model (`kompress-v2-base`, Apache-2.0) served as pre-built ONNX on CPU. obleth still owns all the logic (sentence
splitting, keep-selection, the token-gain gate, the Redis stash, and the
`retrieve_original` machinery); the sidecar **only scores sentences**.

It keeps every guarantee of the boon:

- **Extractive** — it selects existing sentences, never rewrites or fabricates text.
- **Reversible** — the original is stashed in Redis exactly as with the heuristic path.
- **Fail-open** — if the sidecar is unset, times out, or errors, obleth silently
  uses the built-in heuristic. Enabling it never fails or degrades a request.
- **On your own infrastructure** — the model runs in a container you deploy; no
  request text ever leaves your cluster.

It is gated by the same tenant `allow_lossy` opt-in as the heuristic prose pass —
there is no extra tenant toggle. The operator switch is simply deploying the
sidecar and pointing obleth at it.

**Docker Compose.** Add `compressor` to `COMPOSE_PROFILES` and set the URL in
`deploy/docker/.env`:

```bash
COMPOSE_PROFILES=benchmark,edge,observability,compressor
OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL=http://compressor:8080
# OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_TIMEOUT_MS=

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A **boon** is a capability obleth grants a model at the gateway, on top of what
the model can do on its own. Instead of every model needing native support for
every modality — or every caller wiring up extra plumbing — obleth detects when
a request needs a capability the target model lacks, fulfils it at the gateway,
and rewrites the request (and, where needed, the response) so the original model
can answer.

There are six boons, all built on the same engine and opted into through a
model's `boons` list (a fixed vocabulary):

| Boon | `boons` value | Grants | Rewrites |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[Vision](#the-vision-boon)** | `vision` | Image input on a text-only model, by relaying images to a describer model | Request |
| **[Structured output](#the-structured-output-boon)** | `structured_output` | `response_format` JSON-schema adherence | Request + response |
| **[Compression](#the-compression-boon)** | `compression` | Token reduction (structural JSON/code compaction, dedup, deterministic lossy text) before dispatch | Request |
| **[Knowledge](#the-knowledge-boon)** | `knowledge` | Retrieval from admin-curated document collections (RAG), from an in-process vector index, injected ahead of the conversation | Request |
| **[Image generation](#the-image-generation-boon)** | `image_generation` | A gateway-executed `generate_image` tool backed by a registered image model | Request + response |
| **[Speculation](#the-speculation-boon)** | `speculation` | A draft-verify cascade:

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Prerequisites
chunks.text:
You need two models registered:

1. A **describer** — a vision-capable chat model. Give it the `vision` tag (or
   set `supports_vision: true` via the API).
2. One or more **target** models that lack native vision (`supports_vision:
   false`, the default) that you opt into the vision boon.

Register a describer:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "glm-4-5v",
    "model_type": "chat",
    "upstream_model": "glm-4-5v",
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "api_key": "sk_upstream",
    "tags": ["vision"],
    "supports_vision": true,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`supports_vision` is a capability flag on every chat model. It defaults to
`false`, so existing routes need no changes. In the dashboard it is **derived
from the `vision` routing tag** (**Models** → **Routing tags** → **vision**) —
ticking `vision` marks the model as natively image-capable and eligible to serve
as a system-wide describer. The Management API still accepts `supports_vision`
directly.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Relationship to multi-modal routes
chunks.text:
The vision boon is distinct from registering a natively vision-capable chat
model. If a model can see images itself, give it the `vision` tag (which sets
`supports_vision: true`) and the boon leaves its requests alone. The boon exists
specifically to extend **text-only** models that opt in. For serving images,
audio, and embeddings as first-class modalities, see
[Multi-modal Models](/docs/guides/multi-modal-models).

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: `retrieve_original` (a bonus, not a requirement)
chunks.text:
When dedup or the lossy pass replaces a segment, obleth first stores the
**original** in Redis (keyed by a content hash, with a TTL) and leaves a
`[ref:HASH]` marker in its place. **If** the model supports function calling and
the [gateway tool loop](#the-gateway-tool-loop) is enabled, obleth also injects a
gateway-executed `retrieve_original` tool plus a short system note, so the model
can recover the full text on demand — the call is a Redis lookup executed at the
gateway, never forwarded upstream or to the client. On a model without function
calling the compaction still happens; only the recovery tool is omitted.

The original is always stashed **before** the segment is replaced (and only once
the segment is confirmed to actually shrink); if the stash fails, the segment is
left verbatim. A lookup miss (expired TTL, unknown hash) returns a clear "no
longer available" message rather than failing the request.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Streaming, errors, and billing
chunks.text:
- **Streamed live or buffered.** Unlike the structured-output boon, the tool loop
  can stream the final answer **live, token-by-token**; only the tool execution
  between turns pauses the stream. Non-streaming clients get the buffered answer.
- **Fail-open.** A tool error becomes a text result the model can read and recover
  from. A dispatch failure returns the last completion with an
  `x-obleth-boons-warning`. The loop never fails a request outright.
- **Clients that bring their own `tools`** (agentic clients, IDE assistants) keep
  control of them: the granted MCP tools are *merged* into the client's set, the
  gateway executes only its own tools, and any client-owned tool call is handed
  straight back to the client untouched.
- **Billing.** Each model round trip inside the loop is metered against the tenant
  as a `tool_loop` usage record. Tool-loop answers are **never cached**.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The compression boon
chunks.text:
The **compression** boon reduces the number of tokens a model has to *read* —
tool outputs, JSON, code, and bloated replayed history — **before the request is
dispatched upstream**. Savings are measured before upstream billing, so they cut
cost and latency for every client with no client-side changes.

Compression has four pieces, layered from always-safe to opt-in:

| Piece | What it does | Lossless? |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural JSON** | Rewrite a JSON array of like objects as a compact `OBLETH_TABLE` (schema header + CSV rows); fall back to whitespace minification | Lossless — reconstruct-validated, always on when the boon is enabled |
| **Code compaction** | Strip trailing whitespace and collapse blank-line runs in fenced code | Conservative, opt-in (`code_compaction`) |
| **Cross-turn dedup** | Replace a large block repeated across messages with a `[ref:HASH]` marker | Opt-in (`dedup`); original recoverable |
| **Lossy text** | Compact long prose (salience-based sentence extraction) and logs (template collapse). Prose uses a built-in deterministic heuristic by default, or a trained extractive scorer when the [compressor sidecar](#neural-prose-scoring-optional-compressor-sidecar) is deployed | Lossy, opt-in (`allow_lossy`) |

The dedup and lossy passes are **deterministic** and, out of the box, never call
a helper model or touch the network on the request path. The one optional
exception is neural prose scoring: if you deploy the
[compressor sidecar](#neural-prose-scorin

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The gateway tool loop
chunks.text:
The **gateway tool loop** gives a model *actual tools*, not just the tool-calling
capability. When an operator grants a model access to one or more registered
[MCP servers](/docs/guides/mcp-gateway), obleth injects those servers' tools into
the model's chat requests, **executes** the model's tool calls against the MCP
upstream itself, appends the results, and re-asks the model — looping (bounded)
until the model produces a final answer. The client sends a plain OpenAI chat
request and gets a grounded answer back; it never has to run a tool itself.

```text
client ──▶ obleth                         (plain chat request, no tools)
             │  model granted MCP servers + native function calling
             │  inject discovered tools, add the nudge
             ├──▶ target model             "I should search…" → tool_calls
             │  execute tool calls against the MCP server(s)
             ├──▶ MCP server               tools/call → result
             │  append results, re-ask
             ├──▶ target model             (loops up to max_turns)
             │◀── final answer
client ◀─────┘                            grounded answer (no tool_calls)
```

This is a distinct mechanism from the vision boon above. **Capabilities vs tools:**
a *capability* is what a model does natively (function calling); a *tool* is
something registered at the gateway (an MCP server). The vision and structured-
output boons add a capability a model lacks; the tool loop hands real tools to a
mode

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The image generation boon
chunks.text:
The **image_generation** boon lets a chat model produce pictures. obleth merges
a `generate_image` function tool into the model's chat requests; when the model
calls it, the gateway executes the call itself against a registered
[`image`-type model](/docs/guides/multi-modal-models#image-generation) (an
OpenAI-compatible `/images/generations` endpoint, no MCP server involved) and
attaches the result to the model's final reply. An ordinary chat client gets an
image back with no client changes, on both the buffered and the streaming path.

```text
client ──▶ obleth                              (plain chat request)
             │  inject generate_image tool
             ├──▶ target model                 → tool_call generate_image(prompt, size, n)
             ├──▶ image model                  /images/generations (b64_json)
             │  tool result = short text receipt (never the image bytes)
             ├──▶ target model                 final answer
client ◀─────┘                                 answer + image attached as markdown
```

The tool's return value to the model is a short text receipt (for example
`Generated 1 image (1024x1024) for prompt "…"`), so the image never enters the
prompt of the next turn. The image travels out of band and is appended to the
final assistant message as a markdown image with a data URL.

When a client replays that message in a later request, the gateway strips the
attached image bytes back out and replaces them with a compact marker such as

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The knowledge boon
chunks.text:
The **knowledge** boon grounds chat answers on documents you upload. Admins
upload text, Markdown, and CSV files into **collections** (the dashboard's
**Knowledge** page), which are chunked and embedded through a registered
[embedding model](/docs/guides/multi-modal-models#embeddings). A model granted
`knowledge` and attached to one or more collections has the most relevant
passages retrieved for each request and placed ahead of the conversation, from
an in-process vector index. The client sends a plain chat request and gets a
grounded answer.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The speculation boon
chunks.text:
The **speculation** boon is a draft-verify cascade. A fast drafter model writes
the answer, and a scoring deployment of the target model checks every draft
token in one prefill using `prompt_logprobs` before anything reaches the client.
A draft that passes is shipped; one that does not falls through to the target
model, so the client always receives an answer the target model has verified or
written.

- It runs only when the boon is enabled globally, the target model has opted
  into `speculation`, a drafter resolves (the model's own `draft_model`, or the
  fleet default), and a scoring endpoint resolves (the model's own
  `verify_api_base`, or the fleet URL template).
- Requests the cascade cannot honor (multimodal content, `response_format`,
  `logit_bias`, logprobs parameters, audio output) and internal probe keys are
  never drafted.
- Every failure before the first verified span is released (a draft error, a
  verify error, a failed gate, or the pre-release timeout) makes the boon
  abstain, and the request continues down the normal dispatch path.
- Draft and verify calls are metered against the tenant as `speculation_draft`
  and `speculation_verify` usage rows.

It is configured per target model (its drafter and scoring endpoint) and under
**Settings → Boons → Speculation**. Gates, streaming behaviour, category
routing, and the scoring URL template are covered in
[Speculative Drafting](/docs/guides/speculation).

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The structured output boon
chunks.text:
The **structured_output** boon enforces `response_format` JSON schemas at the
gateway for a model without native support. The schema is rendered into the
prompt, the reply is validated at the gateway, and invalid JSON is repaired by a
configurable fixer model — so callers reliably get schema-conforming JSON even
from a model that would otherwise return prose-wrapped or malformed output.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: The vision boon
chunks.text:
When a text-only model receives a chat request that contains an image, the
vision boon:

1. Detects the `image_url` content part(s) in the request.
2. Relays each image to a configured **describer** model — a vision-capable model
   such as `glm-4-5v`.
3. Replaces the image part inline with the returned text, as
   `[Image description: …]`.
4. Forwards the rewritten, now text-only request to the originally requested
   model.

The target model never sees the image bytes; it sees a faithful text description
in their place and answers as if it could see.

```text
client ──▶ obleth                                  (chat request with image_url)
             │  target lacks vision + boon enabled
             ├──▶ describer (glm-4-5v)             "describe this image"
             │◀── "A 3D voxel render of…"
             │  image part → "[Image description: …]"
             ├──▶ target model (text-only)         (rewritten, text-only request)
             │◀── answer
client ◀─────┘                                     answer
```

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Using it from a client
chunks.text:
Send a normal OpenAI-style chat request with an image to a **text-only** model.
No client changes are required — the boon is transparent.

```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "minimax-m2-7-fast",
    "messages": [{
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {"type": "text", "text": "What is this?"},
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."}}
      ]
    }]
  }'
```

obleth relays the image to the describer, rewrites the request, and the
text-only `minimax-m2-7-fast` answers. The request log shows two entries: a
`vision_boon` call against `glm-4-5v`, and the `chat` call against
`minimax-m2-7-fast`.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Verifying
chunks.text:
After a request, confirm the boon ran by looking for the `vision_boon` record in
the usage ledger:

```sql
SELECT toDateTime(ts_ms / 1000) AS t, model, request_type, status_code
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE request_type = 'vision_boon'
ORDER BY ts_ms DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

If you see the target model return errors but **no** `vision_boon` record, the
boon did not fire — re-check the conditions under
[When it applies](#when-it-applies): the boon is enabled, a describer is set, the
target model has opted in (`boons` includes `vision`), and it is flagged
`supports_vision: false`.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: Web search end to end
chunks.text:
A common use of the tool loop is giving a model **live web search**. The
`examples/searxng/` compose file runs a private
[SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) metasearch instance fronted by an MCP server,
both joined to obleth's docker network:

```bash
docker compose -f examples/searxng/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

Register the MCP server in obleth (**MCP Servers → Register**, or the API) with
upstream URL `http://mcp-searxng:8765/mcp`, grant it to a function-calling model's
`tool_servers`, and enable the loop. From then on the model can run live web
searches mid-conversation — the client just asks a question and obleth handles the
search, the tool call, and the follow-up turn. See the
[MCP Gateway](/docs/guides/mcp-gateway#the-gateway-tool-loop) guide for the full
walkthrough.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
The boon runs for a request only when **all** of the following hold:

- The vision boon is **enabled** globally.
- A **describer model** is configured.
- The target model has **opted into** the vision boon (its `boons` list includes
  `vision`). Boons are off by default and granted per model — obleth never
  applies a boon to a model that hasn't asked for it.
- The target model is **not** flagged `supports_vision` (models that can see
  images are left untouched — their images pass straight through).
- The request actually contains an `image_url` content part.

If any condition is false, the request is forwarded unchanged.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
The loop runs for a request only when **all** of the following hold:

- The gateway tool loop is **enabled** globally.
- The target model has one or more MCP servers granted via its `tool_servers`
  list.
- The target model **is** flagged `supports_function_calling`. A model that is
  granted tool servers but lacks native function calling gets **no** tools
  injected, and obleth logs a loud warning — enable function calling on the model
  to use the loop.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
- The structured-output boon is **enabled** globally.
- The target model has **opted into** `structured_output` and is **not** flagged
  `supports_response_schema`.
- The request is a **chat completion** whose `response_format.type` is
  `json_schema` or `json_object`.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
Like every boon, compression is **opt-in twice** — enabled globally **and**
granted to the model via its `boons` list (`compression`). Beyond that, each
piece is gated independently:

- **Structural JSON** runs whenever the boon is enabled for the model and the
  tenant hasn't opted out (chat completions only; internal probe keys are
  exempt).
- **Code compaction** runs only when `code_compaction` is on — globally as the
  default, or per tenant.
- **Cross-turn dedup** and **lossy text** require the tenant to opt in (`dedup` /
  `allow_lossy`). They are **model-free and run on any model** — there is no
  function-calling or tool-loop requirement.

Compression targets **any large segment**: the latest user message (so a "here's
a huge file, now answer" turn is compacted), older history, and tool outputs. The
**only** thing never modified is a **trailing assistant message**. Segments below
`min_tokens` are always left alone.

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
- The knowledge boon is **enabled** globally (**Settings → Knowledge**, or
  `PUT /api/v1/settings/knowledge`).
- The target model has **opted into** `knowledge` *and* has one or more
  collections attached (`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/models/{id}/knowledge`, or the
  model's **Knowledge** section in the dashboard).
- The request is a chat completion from a key that is not an internal probe key.

The retrieval query is captured from the untouched messages before any
compression pass, and the retrieved block is injected after compression and
after the tenant's input guardrails scan, so it reaches the model verbatim.
Applied requests carry `knowledge` in `x-obleth-boons`.

It is off by default and fails open: no embedder, an embedding timeout, an
empty index, or nothing scoring above the similarity floor leaves the request
untouched. Collections, retrieval settings, and the indexing lifecycle are
covered in [Knowledge Base (RAG)](/docs/guides/knowledge-base).

chunks.title: Model Boons
chunks.heading: When it applies
chunks.text:
- The image generation boon is **enabled** globally and an **image model** is
  set.
- The target model has **opted into** `image_generation`.
- The target model **is** flagged `supports_function_calling`. A model granted
  the boon without native function calling gets no tool, and obleth logs a
  warning.

There is no per-tenant opt-out: granting the boon to a model is the opt-in. It
does not depend on the MCP tool loop's global switch: granting a model the
ability to draw works whether or not the tool loop is enabled.

A client that already defines its own `generate_image` tool keeps it — the
gateway does not inject its tool and leaves the client's tool calls to the
client. The same applies when a granted MCP server already exposes a tool of
that name. In both cases obleth logs a warning and the boon is inactive for that
request.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: A config fix takes effect immediately
chunks.text:
Changing a model's `api_base`, `upstream_model`, or `model_type` resets its
health state — status back to `unknown`, failure streak zeroed, alert state
cleared, and the next check scheduled for now — so a fixed route re-verifies
within one worker tick instead of carrying a stale "down" badge. Check history
rows are kept.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Alerts
chunks.text:
Health alerts go out through the channels configured in **Settings → Alerts**
(Slack incoming webhook and email, with a shared delivery cooldown). See
[Alerting](/docs/operations/alerting). `OBLETH_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and
`OBLETH_SLACK_ALERT_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS` only seed those settings on first boot,
before anything has been saved from the dashboard.

Each model has its own failure threshold, default `2`. obleth sends one down
alert when the threshold is reached and a recovery alert when the model becomes
healthy again.

The **health badge tracks the same threshold** as the alert: a model only reads
`unhealthy` once it has crossed its failure threshold — not on the latest single
probe — so the badge flips exactly when an alert would fire rather than flickering
on one bad check. Combined with the active probe's extra retry-with-backoff, a
brief blip (common on cold Slurm nodes) doesn't register as down at all.

Alerts are suppressed when:

- alerts are disabled for that model;
- the model is in an active maintenance window; or
- the route itself is disabled.

Failed checks are still stored during maintenance, so the history remains useful
after the window ends.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Classification
chunks.text:
The probe makes up to **three attempts** (one try plus two retries with
exponential backoff) on `408`/`429`/`5xx` or a network error before recording a
result. The final outcome maps as:

| Probe outcome | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `2xx` | `healthy` |
| `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `422` | `unhealthy` |
| `408`, `429`, `5xx`, any other code | `degraded` |
| Transport error / unreachable | `unhealthy` |

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Configuration mistakes are not outages
chunks.text:
A `400`/`404`/`422` rejection means either "the model is gone" or "wrong endpoint
for this modality". obleth disambiguates against the upstream catalog:

- the catalog **lists** the model → `degraded`, with a message naming the
  endpoint that rejected it and pointing at `model_type`. It does not count
  toward failure alerts.
- the catalog **does not list** it → `unhealthy`, with the catalog as evidence.
- the catalog is a **wildcard** or unreachable → the original result stands
  unchanged. A wildcard adds no information and may never confirm health.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Dashboard

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Manual checks
chunks.text:
Run one check:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/health/check \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Run checks for eligible models:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/health \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Bulk checks skip routes that are disabled, hidden for maintenance, or have
checks disabled.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Models with no static `api_base` (dynamic endpoints)
chunks.text:
[Slurm-provisioned models](/docs/guides/slurm-provisioning) have no static
`api_base` — their live URLs live entirely in the endpoint pool, which changes as
replicas come and go. For these, the model-level status is **derived from the
endpoint pool** instead of from an empty base. An endpoint counts as *serving*
when its probe came back `healthy` or `degraded` (that is, reachable), and the
pool is graded against the managed spec's `min_replicas`:

| Pool | Model status |
| --- | --- |
| serving ≥ `min_replicas` | `healthy` |
| 0 < serving < `min_replicas` | `degraded` (below the floor) |
| every live endpoint `unknown` | `unknown` (unverified, non-alerting) |
| no live endpoints registered, or all unreachable | `unhealthy` |

A recent passive success may only settle a pool that **still has a live endpoint
serving**. Once every replica has gone away, a success recorded just before they
died is stale, and the pool reports its own reality instead of riding that `2xx`
to `healthy`.

Because the endpoints are probed from the gateway, a Slurm replica that the
provisioner promoted can still report `unhealthy` here if the gateway itself
cannot reach the node — see the
[Slurm troubleshooting notes](/docs/guides/slurm-provisioning#troubleshooting).

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Model health checks judge each registered route with the cheapest trustworthy
signal available, in order:

1. **Passive** — a recent real `2xx` for that model in the ClickHouse usage
   ledger. Free, and as good as a probe: the model demonstrably served.
2. **Active minimal inference** — a real forward pass against the endpoint the
   model's `model_type` actually serves (a one-token chat completion, a
   one-string embedding, one character of speech, a 0.1-second silence clip to
   transcribe).
3. **Catalog existence** — for types with no cheap inference probe (`image`, and
   any unrecognized type), `GET {api_base}/models` membership. If `/models`
   returns `404`, the probe retries `/models/` with a trailing slash,
   so gateways that mount their catalog only there (AIBrix's metadata service,
   for example) are still read.

Active probes are *real* requests, so they consume a negligible number of
upstream tokens. Those tokens are recorded under the internal nil tenant
(`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`) with `request_type = health_probe`, so
probe traffic never lands on a client's bill, stays out of usage stats by
default, and is hidden from the request log.

A healthy result covers the parts that matter to operators:

- the model registry lookup and route configuration;
- the configured upstream being reachable; and
- the upstream actually accepting a real request for the route's
  `upstream_model` on the endpoint its `model_type` implies.

Transient conditions — an

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Passive signal vs active probe
chunks.text:
| Source | When used | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive (ClickHouse `usage`) | The model had at least one `2xx` in the window | `healthy` |
| Active probe | No observed success in the window | `healthy`/`degraded`/`unhealthy`/`unknown` from the probe |

The passive window follows the model's own **check interval**, with a floor of
300 seconds — so at the default 900-second interval a model with steady traffic
is settled for free instead of probed. Only an observed **success**
short-circuits the probe. Recent errors are deliberately not trusted as a
verdict: they may be stale, and acting on them would suppress the very probe
whose success would clear them, pinning a recovered model at `unhealthy` until
the window aged out. Anything short of an observed success falls through to a
live probe as ground truth.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Per-endpoint health
chunks.text:
When a model defines multiple [endpoints](/docs/guides/reliability-and-failover),
the worker probes **each enabled endpoint independently** with the same
per-modality probe and records a per-endpoint `health_status`. Disabled endpoints
are recorded as `disabled` without a network call. The data plane only routes to
endpoints that are enabled and neither `unhealthy` nor `disabled` — `unknown` and
`degraded` soft-pass — so a dead cluster drops out of rotation on its own while
the rest of the model keeps serving.

A `degraded` endpoint probe lifts a stale `unhealthy` (it is still a real
liveness signal) but never downgrades a confirmed `healthy`, so an endpoint that
is reachable but whose upstream id doesn't appear in its `/v1/models` list can
recover into rotation on its own.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Pre-flight validation
chunks.text:
`POST /api/v1/models/validate` answers, without writing anything, whether an
upstream is reachable, whether its catalog is a wildcard pass-through, and
whether it lists a given `upstream_model`. It fetches the catalog uncached (so an
operator who just registered a model upstream sees current truth) and with the
same trailing-slash retry as the health checks, so creating a model against a
healthy AIBrix-style backend no longer fails validation. The dashboard calls it
when you create or edit a model and surfaces the returned `warnings`; a save is
never blocked by it.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/validate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "upstream_model": "meta-llama/Llama-3-70b-instruct",
    "model_type": "chat"
  }'
```

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Scheduled checks
chunks.text:
The worker is enabled by default:

```bash
OBLETH_MODEL_HEALTH_ENABLED=true
OBLETH_MODEL_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECS=900
OBLETH_MODEL_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SECS=30
OBLETH_MODEL_HEALTH_RETENTION_DAYS=30
```

Checks are claimed with Postgres row locking, so multiple Management API
replicas can run safely without a single in-memory leader. Per-model jitter keeps
large fleets from checking every route at once.

Health state is stored in Postgres, so a gateway restart keeps each model's last
known status. The data plane's routing refresh also keeps the last known health
when a health query fails, so a failed query never re-enables an unhealthy model
or one under maintenance.

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: Statuses
chunks.text:
| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `healthy` | The model served a real request, or had recent successful client traffic. |
| `degraded` | Reachable but not confirmed serving — overload, an inconclusive response, or a probe rejection the upstream catalog attributes to configuration. Non-alerting on its own. |
| `unhealthy` | Actionable: the model is missing upstream, credentials were rejected, or the upstream is unreachable. Counts toward the failure threshold. |
| `unknown` | Nothing could be verified — for example a wildcard (`"*"`) upstream catalog, which can never confirm that a model exists. Never reported as healthy. |
| `disabled` | The route itself is disabled; no network call is made. |

chunks.title: Model Health
chunks.heading: What the active probe sends
chunks.text:
| `model_type` | Probe |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | `POST {api_base}/chat/completions` — one `ping` message, `max_tokens: 1` |
| `embedding` | `POST {api_base}/embeddings` — `input: "ping"` |
| `audio_speech` | `POST {api_base}/audio/speech` — `input: "."`, `voice: "alloy"` |
| `audio_transcription` | multipart `POST {api_base}/audio/transcriptions` — a generated 0.1 s silent WAV |
| `image`, unrecognized | `GET {api_base}/models` existence check (a "minimal" image generation is still costly) |

Probing each type against its own endpoint is what keeps embedding, TTS, and
transcription routes from being rejected by a chat endpoint and left sitting
falsely `degraded`. Catalog lookups are cached per `api_base` for 60 seconds, so
a sweep across many models sharing one upstream lists it once.

Catalog fetches try both spellings of the URL: `{api_base}/models` first and,
**only on a 404**, `{api_base}/models/` with a trailing slash. Some gateways —
AIBrix's metadata service among them — mount their catalog only at `/v1/models/`
with slash redirects off, so the canonical path 404s with no redirect to follow;
without the retry every model behind such a gateway reported an unreachable
catalog. On failure the error names the configured spelling, so the message
points at a URL you can actually check.

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Aliases
chunks.text:
An alias is another name that resolves to the same route. Aliases let a model
carry a clean name while clients that pinned an older spelling keep working:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "glm-5-3",
    "aliases": ["glm-5-3-mxfp4"],
    "upstream_model": "zai-org/GLM-5.3-MXFP4",
    "api_base": "https://inference.example.com/v1",
    "quantization": "mxfp4"
  }'
```

`model_name` cannot be changed on an existing route, and an alias cannot reuse
a name another route still holds. To rename a route, delete it and create the
new one with the old name as an alias; requests naming the old name fail
between the two steps.

- An alias resolves in the same single lookup as the canonical name, so it
  costs nothing per request.
- Requests made by alias are recorded under the canonical `model_name`, and
  tenant allowlists, fairshare pools, and budgets all use the canonical name.
  Usage is not split across spellings.
- Discovery endpoints advertise only `model_name`. `GET /v1/models` entries and
  `/model/info` list the aliases that still resolve.
- Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Blank and duplicate entries are
  dropped, and a model keeps at most 16 aliases.
- An alias cannot equal the model's own name, another model's name or alias,
  or the reserved name `auto`. The write is rejected with 400 naming the
  conflict.
- On update, `aliases` replaces

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Auto routing
chunks.text:
- `auto_eligible: false` removes the model from `auto`'s candidates. It stays
  addressable by name. The routing explanation lists it under `auto_excluded`.
  This differs from `enabled: false`, which removes it everywhere.
- `route_bias` multiplies the model's final auto-router score. `1.0` is
  neutral; the value is clamped to 0.1 to 3.0 when scoring.

See [Auto Model Routing](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing) for the scoring.

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Capability flags and context window
chunks.text:
The auto router drops a model that cannot serve a request: one whose
`context_window` is smaller than the prompt estimate plus `max_tokens` (a
window of `0` is treated as unknown and never excludes), or that lacks function
calling, tool choice, a JSON response schema, or vision when the request needs
them. The structured-output and vision boons count as the matching capability.
The `/v1/messages` surface also clamps `max_tokens` to `context_window`, so an
accurate window matters for Anthropic clients.

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Export and import the registry
chunks.text:
The registry can be written to an **`obleth-models` manifest** and applied
back, on the same instance or another. The manifest is meant to be read,
edited by hand, and kept in a repository. It is separate from the
[config backup](/docs/operations/backup-restore), which is a whole-instance
disaster-recovery file keyed by id.

In the dashboard, the Models page has **Export** and **Import** buttons.
Through the Management API:

```bash
# Export every model (JSON)
curl -s http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/export \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > obleth-models.json

# Preview an import without writing anything
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/import?dry_run=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @obleth-models.json

# Apply it
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/import \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @obleth-models.json
```

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Format
chunks.text:
```yaml
format: obleth-models
version: 1
models:
  - model_name: glm-5-3
    aliases: [glm-5-3-mxfp4]
    upstream_model: zai-org/GLM-5.3-MXFP4
    api_base: https://inference.example.com/v1
    quantization: mxfp4
    context_window: 131072
    input_cost_per_token: 0.0000006
    output_cost_per_token: 0.0000022
    supports_function_calling: true
    supports_tool_choice: true
    tags: [coding, "reasoning:3"]
    endpoints:
      - name: primary
        api_base: https://inference.example.com/v1
        priority: 100
        weight: 100

  # Sparse entries touch only what they name: this one retags an existing model.
  - model_name: qwen3-embedding-8b
    tags: [general]
```

- **Keyed by `model_name`.** A name that exists is updated; a new name is
  created. Models not in the file are left alone. Import never deletes.
- **Sparse.** Every field except `model_name` is optional, and an absent field
  means "leave unchanged" (or the default when creating). The fields are the
  route fields listed above, except the read-only ones.
- **No secrets on export.** Export writes `has_api_key: true|false` instead of
  the key, so a manifest is safe to commit. `has_api_key` is ignored on import.
  An import may set `api_key` in plain text; an empty string clears it; an
  absent key is left untouched.
- **Endpoints** are matched by `name` within the model. Endpoints missing from
  the list are never deleted; omitting `endpoints` leaves them all alone.
- `max_in_flight` and `request_time

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: `GET /model/info`
chunks.text:
A data-plane endpoint (also at `/v1/model/info`) that reports what the gateway
was configured with, served from the registry rather than the upstreams. It
lists every enabled route whether or not its backend answers at the moment.
Tenants with a model allowlist see only the models they may call. Upstream URLs
and keys are never included.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"
```

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "model_name": "glm-5-3",
      "obleth_params": {"model": "zai-org/GLM-5.3-MXFP4"},
      "model_info": {
        "mode": "chat",
        "max_input_tokens": 131072,
        "input_cost_per_token": 0.0000006,
        "output_cost_per_token": 0.0000022,
        "supports_function_calling": true,
        "supports_system_messages": true,
        "supports_response_schema": true,
        "supports_vision": false,
        "model_type": "chat",
        "quantization": "mxfp4",
        "aliases": ["glm-5-3-mxfp4"],
        "tags": ["coding", "reasoning"],
        "boons": [],
        "supports_tool_choice": true,
        "context_window": 131072,
        "cost_per_image": 0.0,
        "cost_per_audio_second": 0.0,
        "cost_per_character": 0.0,
        "healthy": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`obleth_params.model` is the upstream model name. `mode` follows the LiteLLM
convention (`image` is spelled `image_generation`); `healthy` is the gateway's
last observed health. Where `GET /v1/models` answers "what can I call right
no

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Every model a client can call is a **route** in the gateway's registry: a
client-facing `model_name` mapped to an upstream `api_base` and
`upstream_model`, plus the pricing, capability, routing, and reliability
settings the gateway applies to it. Routes are stored in Postgres, pushed to
Redis for the data plane, and managed from the dashboard **Models** page or the
[Management API](/docs/reference/management-api) (`/api/v1/models`).

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Quantization
chunks.text:
`quantization` records the weight or activation format a deployment serves.
It is descriptive only: it never affects routing. Keeping it out of the name
means re-quantizing a deployment is an edit, not a rename.

Vocabulary: `unknown` (the default: nobody declared it), `none` (deliberately
unquantized), `fp16`, `bf16`, `fp8`, `nvfp4`, `mxfp4`, `int8`, `int4`, `awq`,
`gptq`, `gguf`.

Values are matched case-insensitively. The create and update routes and a
manifest import reject anything outside the vocabulary with 400; an empty
value means `unknown`. [Provider import](/docs/guides/import-models) reads the
format off a discovered model id and suggests it for you.

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Route fields
chunks.text:
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model_name` | required | The name clients send in `model`. Unique. Keep it free of deployment detail |
| `aliases` | `[]` | Extra names that resolve to this route (see [Aliases](#aliases)) |
| `description` | `""` | Operator-facing summary |
| `upstream_model` | required | The value sent upstream in the `model` field |
| `api_base` | required | The provider base URL, ending in `/v1` when the provider needs it |
| `api_key` | none | Upstream credential. Write-only: responses carry `api_key_set` instead |
| `model_type` | `chat` | `chat`, `embedding`, `audio_transcription`, `audio_speech`, or `image` (see [Multi-modal Models](/docs/guides/multi-modal-models)) |
| `quantization` | `unknown` | Serving format (see [Quantization](#quantization)) |
| `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token` | `0` | USD per token |
| `cost_per_image`, `cost_per_audio_second`, `cost_per_character` | `0` | USD per unit for non-chat modalities |
| `context_window` | `8192` | Maximum tokens. `0` means unknown |
| `admission_weight` | `100` | Percent factor applied to every caller's weight in this model's pool. It does not change the model's share of capacity (see [Fairshare Engine](/docs/concepts/fairshare-engine#effective-weight)) |
| `max_in_flight` | none | This model's fairshare pool size, the setting that controls its concurrency. Unset uses `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` |
| `capacity_mode` | `static` | `static`, or `tuned` when set

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Tags
chunks.text:
Routing tags describe what a chat model is good at and steer the
[auto router](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing). The vocabulary is fixed:

```
coding · general · reasoning · math · vision · long-context · fast · creative
```

A tag can carry a strength level, `tag:1`, `tag:2`, or `tag:3`, used by the
auto router's difficulty tiering. A bare tag leaves the level to be derived.
Unknown tags are dropped. In the dashboard, checking the `vision` tag also sets
`supports_vision`.

chunks.title: Model Registry
chunks.heading: Validation and preview
chunks.text:
The whole file is validated before anything is written, and every problem is
reported in one response. Any error rejects the file and nothing changes.

- Rejected: an unknown `model_type`, `quantization`, `capacity_mode`, or
  `endpoint_selection_mode`; a negative cost or `route_bias`; an endpoint
  without an `api_base`; a model or endpoint listed twice; an alias that
  collides with another name (judged against the state the file would
  produce, so a file may move an alias from one model to another); an
  `api_base` or `verify_api_base` blocked by the outbound URL policy.
- Warned, not rejected: unknown tags and boons (dropped), aliases dropped as
  blank, duplicate, or over the cap, and tool servers that are not registered
  (kept; the grant stays inert until the server exists).

The report lists each model as `created`, `updated`, or `unchanged`, with the
fields that change and any warnings. `?dry_run=true` returns the same report
without writing, and the dashboard always shows this preview before you
confirm. Unchanged models are not rewritten.

Export and import are recorded in the [audit log](/docs/operations/audit-log)
as `export_models` and `import_models`.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Core vs optional
chunks.text:
**Core (always on):** Postgres (config source of truth + audit + dashboard
accounts), Redis (hot cache, token budgets, response cache; password required),
ClickHouse (usage ledger), the `obleth` data plane, and the `control-plane`
dashboard.

**Optional:**

| Component | Role | When to enable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `benchmark-backend` | GPU-free benchmark fixture backend | dev / demos only |
| HAProxy / Ingress | TLS termination + round-robin across obleth pods | when you don't already have an edge LB |
| Prometheus + Grafana | metrics scrape + dashboards | when you want in-cluster metrics |
| Jaeger (OTLP collector) | distributed tracing backend | when `OBLETH_OTEL_ENDPOINT` is set |
| `obleth-provisioner` | keeps managed models alive on Slurm | when models run on a Slurm cluster |
| `compressor` | neural prose compression sidecar | when the compression boon should use neural scoring |

Keep HAProxy for self-contained demos; in production replace it with a managed
load balancer (drop the Compose `edge` profile) or a Kubernetes `Ingress` (Helm
`ingress.enabled`).

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Dashboard auth
chunks.text:
```yaml
controlPlane:
  dashboardAdminEmail: admin@example.com
  dashboardPassword: change-me
  dashboardSessionSecret: a-long-random-secret-of-at-least-32-chars
```

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Dependency toggles
chunks.text:
```yaml
postgres:
  enabled: false                 # use an external/operator Postgres
  external:
    url: postgres://user:pass@pg-host:5432/obleth
redis:
  enabled: false
  external:
    url: redis://:REDIS_PASSWORD@redis-host:6379   # single primary
clickhouse:
  enabled: false
  external:
    url: http://clickhouse-host:8123
benchmarkBackend:
  enabled: false                 # production: no bundled benchmark fixture backend
obleth:
  upstreamBaseUrl: https://my-vllm-endpoint/v1
```

When a dependency is `enabled: false`, its `external.url` is **required** — the
chart wires obleth at that URL instead of an in-chart service. Leaving it blank
fails the render with a clear message rather than booting a misconfigured pod.
When the bundled Redis is enabled, `redis.password` is required instead.

After `helm install`, register models and mint tenant keys — the chart does not
do this for you. See [Installation — post-install steps](/docs/getting-started/installation#post-install-steps-kubernetes).

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Docker Compose profiles
chunks.text:
Profiles gate the optional services. Core services have no profile and always
start.

```bash
# Lean core only (point obleth at a real upstream, see below)
docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml up

# Full dev/demo stack
docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml \
  --profile benchmark --profile edge --profile observability up
```

Or default the profiles on by setting `COMPOSE_PROFILES` in
`deploy/docker/.env` (copy from `.env.example`):

```bash
COMPOSE_PROFILES=benchmark,edge,observability
```

| Profile | Services |
| --- | --- |
| `benchmark` | `benchmark-backend` |
| `mock` | legacy alias for `benchmark` |
| `edge` | `haproxy` |
| `observability` | `prometheus`, `grafana`, `jaeger`, `postgres-exporter`, `redis-exporter` |
| `slurm` | `obleth-provisioner` |
| `compressor` | `compressor` (neural prose compression sidecar) |
| `sso-dev` | `dex` (local OIDC provider for dashboard SSO development) |

The `compressor` profile builds an image that bakes a ~600 MB ONNX model, so its
first build is slow and needs network access. It stays off unless you list it in
`COMPOSE_PROFILES`. Enabling it also requires pointing obleth at the sidecar with
`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL=http://compressor:8080`; without that URL the feature stays off
even when the container is running. The sidecar image is tagged by
`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` (default `latest`) rather than `OBLETH_VERSION`,
because edge builds do not publish it. Leave it on a release tag when
`OBLETH_VERSION` tr

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Helm
chunks.text:
The chart bundles dependencies for a self-contained install and lets you swap any
of them for an external/operator-managed endpoint. Image tags left empty
(`image.tag: ""`, the default) resolve to `v{appVersion}` from `Chart.yaml`: a
chart at version 1.3.0 pulls the `v1.3.0` images, so upgrading the chart
upgrades the images without editing a tag.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Ingress (HAProxy's k8s equivalent)
chunks.text:
```yaml
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx
  host: obleth.example.com
  servicePort: 8080
  tls:
    - secretName: obleth-tls
      hosts: [obleth.example.com]
```

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Network policy
chunks.text:
`networkPolicy.enabled: true` renders NetworkPolicies (it needs a CNI that
enforces them): the bundled Postgres admits the obleth and dashboard pods, the
bundled Redis and ClickHouse admit only the obleth pods, and the obleth
Management API port (9180) admits only the dashboard and provisioner pods. The
data-plane (8080) and metrics (9091) ports stay open.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Neural prose compression sidecar
chunks.text:
Off by default. Enable it to run the `compressor` scoring service and wire obleth at
it automatically (`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL` is injected for you). The sidecar is
stateless, so it scales horizontally.

**Scale with small pods, not fat ones.** The scorer is CPU-only (no GPU needed) but
CPU-hungry, and its throughput does **not** grow with pod size: a single inference
saturates at about **4 cores** (measured on the default model — 4 cores ≈ 105
sentences/s, 8/16/24 cores barely more). Giving a pod 32 cores wastes 28 of them.
Because each pod also holds the ~900 MB model resident in RAM, very small pods
multiply memory. So the sweet spot is **~4 cores per pod, then add replicas** for
aggregate throughput. Keep `numThreads` equal to the CPU limit so each replica
cleanly owns its cores, and turn on `autoscaling` under variable load.

```yaml
compressor:
  enabled: true
  # Aggregate throughput comes from replicas, not big pods. On a CPU-rich cluster,
  # e.g. replicas: 24 with 4 cores each (~2500 sentences/s over ~96 cores) beats a
  # handful of 32-core pods using the same or more cores.
  replicas: 4
  numThreads: 4          # keep small (~4); == limits.cpu
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "4", memory: 1536Mi }
    limits:   { cpu: "4", memory: 2Gi }
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    minReplicas: 4
    maxReplicas: 24
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
```

CPU-based autoscaling is only meaningful because `resources.limits.cpu` is set —
leave `resources` empty and the s

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth ships as a small core plus optional components. Both the Docker Compose
stack and the Helm chart let you turn pieces on and off so the same artifacts
serve a one-command demo and a lean production install.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Pointing at a real upstream
chunks.text:
The obleth service has no dependency on the benchmark fixture backend. Set the
default upstream in `.env`:

```bash
OBLETH_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL=https://my-vllm-or-aibrix-endpoint/v1
```

Run without the `benchmark` profile and obleth routes straight to your real
inference endpoint. Each registered model's own `api_base` takes precedence.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Shared settings
chunks.text:
`.env.example` documents the keys that must agree across services:

- `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` — shared by `obleth`, `control-plane`, and `obleth-provisioner`.
- `OBLETH_VERSION` — image tag for the first-party services (`latest` tracks the
  newest stable release, `dev` tracks unreleased edge builds; pin `vX.Y.Z` for
  reproducible deploys).
- `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `REDIS_PASSWORD`, `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` — used by the
  bundled datastores and composed into obleth's connection URLs (Redis as
  `redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379`, so keep it URL-safe).
- `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` — default upstream for the data plane.
- `OBLETH_OTEL_ENDPOINT` — OTLP/HTTP collector base URL (empty = tracing off).
- `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` / `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` — break-glass admin login. Add `OIDC_PROVIDERS` (and `BETTER_AUTH_URL`) to enable SSO.

The Compose file fixes some gateway settings (the in-flight ceiling and pool
size, fairshare history and algorithm, fail-open) so `.env` cannot change them.
[Docker Compose](/docs/reference/docker-compose) lists what is forwarded from
`.env` and what is fixed.

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Tracing
chunks.text:
```yaml
obleth:
  otelEndpoint: http://my-collector:4318
```

chunks.title: Modular Deploy
chunks.heading: Values matrix (quick reference)
chunks.text:
| Value | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `postgres.enabled` | `true` | bundle Postgres vs use `postgres.external.url` |
| `redis.enabled` | `true` | bundle Redis vs use `redis.external.url` |
| `redis.password` | `""` | required when `redis.enabled`; URL-safe characters only |
| `clickhouse.enabled` | `true` | bundle ClickHouse vs use `clickhouse.external.url` |
| `benchmarkBackend.enabled` | `true` | bundle benchmark fixture backend (set `false` + `obleth.upstreamBaseUrl` in prod) |
| `ingress.enabled` | `false` | expose obleth through an Ingress |
| `obleth.replicas` | `1` | data-plane replica count; pools and `globalMaxInFlight` are enforced **per replica**, so N replicas admit up to N × each |
| `obleth.globalMaxInFlight` | `1024` | total in-flight ceiling across model pools, per replica |
| `obleth.defaultModelMaxInFlight` | `32` | pool size for a model without its own `max_in_flight` |
| `hpa.enabled` | `false` | autoscale obleth on CPU (moves the aggregate concurrency with the replica count) |
| `podDisruptionBudget.enabled` | `true` | keep pods available during drains; rendered only when the minimum replica count (`hpa.minReplicas` with HPA, else `obleth.replicas`) is greater than 1 |
| `networkPolicy.enabled` | `false` | render the NetworkPolicies described above |
| `serviceMonitor.enabled` | `false` | create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor |
| `obleth.otelEndpoint` | `""` | OTLP/HTTP trace export target |
| `controlPlane.trustedOrigins` | `""` | extr

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Cost fields by modality
chunks.text:
| Field | Applies to | Billing basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input_cost_per_token` | `chat`, `embedding` | Prompt tokens |
| `output_cost_per_token` | `chat` | Completion tokens |
| `cost_per_image` | `image` | Per image (`× n`) |
| `cost_per_character` | `audio_speech` | Per input character |
| `cost_per_audio_second` | `audio_transcription` | Stored and reported, but not applied: transcription requests carry no per-second charge |

All modality costs flow into the same usage ledger and the `GET /api/v1/costs`
breakdown.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Embeddings
chunks.text:
Register an embedding route:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "qwen3-embedding-8b",
    "model_type": "embedding",
    "upstream_model": "Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B",
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "api_key": "sk_upstream",
    "input_cost_per_token": 0.00000001,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

Call it with the OpenAI SDK:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost/v1", api_key="sk_...")

resp = client.embeddings.create(
    model="qwen3-embedding-8b",
    input="The quick brown fox",
)
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))
```

Embeddings are billed on prompt tokens only via `input_cost_per_token`.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Health checks
chunks.text:
Health probes are modality-aware: every scheduled, manual, and bulk check sends a
minimal *real* request to the endpoint the route's `model_type` actually serves,
so a non-chat route is never rejected by a chat endpoint and left falsely
`degraded`.

- `chat` (default) → `POST /v1/chat/completions`, one `ping` message with
  `max_tokens: 1`
- `embedding` → `POST /v1/embeddings` with `input: "ping"`
- `audio_speech` → `POST /v1/audio/speech` with `input: "."` and `voice: "alloy"`
- `audio_transcription` → multipart `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` with a
  generated 0.1-second silent WAV
- `image` → no inference probe (even a minimal generation is costly): obleth
  checks the upstream catalog (`GET {api_base}/models`) for the model id instead

Probe usage is recorded with request type `health_probe` under an internal
tenant, so it never appears on a client's bill. If a probe is rejected but the upstream catalog
still lists the model, obleth reports `degraded` with a pointer at `model_type`
rather than declaring an outage.

See [Model Health](/docs/guides/model-health) for scheduling, alerts, and
maintenance windows.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Image generation
chunks.text:
Image routes serve `/v1/images/generations` (and `edits`/`variations`). Any
OpenAI-compatible image backend works as a pass-through — including
Stable Diffusion servers that expose the OpenAI images API. No adapter is
required.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "sdxl",
    "model_type": "image",
    "upstream_model": "stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0",
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "api_key": "sk_upstream",
    "cost_per_image": 0.02,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

```python
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost/v1", api_key="sk_...")

img = client.images.generate(
    model="sdxl",
    prompt="a watercolor fox",
    n=2,
    size="1024x1024",
)
print(img.data[0].url)
```

Image generation is billed as `n × cost_per_image`.

Only backends that expose the OpenAI images API are supported. Non-OpenAI
graph backends, such as ComfyUI workflows, are not.

A registered `image` route can also back the
[`image_generation` boon](/docs/guides/model-boons#the-image-generation-boon):
grant a chat model the boon and the gateway executes a `generate_image` tool
against your image route, so ordinary chat clients get pictures back
mid-conversation with no client changes.

To exercise an image route directly (prompt, negative prompt, size, count,
steps, seed, with per-result latency and cost), use the Playground's **Image**
workspace

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Importing models
chunks.text:
Both import paths accept `model_type` and the per-modality cost fields:

- An `obleth-models` manifest registers or updates many routes from one file.
  See [Model Registry](/docs/guides/model-registry#export-and-import-the-registry).
- Provider import lists what an OpenAI-compatible provider serves and registers
  the models you pick. See
  [Import Models from a Provider](/docs/guides/import-models).

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Modality on `/v1/models`
chunks.text:
The gateway's aggregated `GET /v1/models` listing annotates every entry that
matches a registered route with `model_type` (obleth's vocabulary), `mode`
(the LiteLLM-convention alias, where `image` is spelled `image_generation`),
`quantization`, `tags`, and `aliases`, so clients can group models by modality
without guessing from the id. Matched entries are also canonicalized onto the
gateway's own `model_name`: a backend that only knows itself by a quantized
spelling like `glm-5-3-mxfp4` is listed once, under the clean name. Upstream
catalogs mounted only at `/v1/models/` (AIBrix-style gateways) are retried with
the trailing slash, so no route drops out of the listing. See
[OpenAI-compatible API](/docs/guides/openai-compatible-api#model-discovery).

For configured facts the backends cannot report (prices, capability flags,
granted boons, last-observed health), use `GET /model/info` (also at
`/v1/model/info`), served from the gateway's own registry with the per-route
facts under `obleth_params`.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Model types
chunks.text:
`model_type` is a field on every model route. It defaults to `chat`, so existing
routes need no changes.

| `model_type` | OpenAI endpoint | Request shape | Auto-routing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat` | `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions` | JSON | Yes |
| `embedding` | `/v1/embeddings` | JSON | No |
| `audio_transcription` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations` | multipart/form-data | No |
| `audio_speech` | `/v1/audio/speech` | JSON | No |
| `image` | `/v1/images/generations` (+ edits/variations) | JSON | No |

Only `chat` routes participate in `auto` model routing. Non-chat routes are
always addressed explicitly by `model_name`, because a TTS request and a chat
request are not interchangeable.

The registry mixes modalities freely — chat and vision models sit alongside
audio transcription (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS) routes, each with its own
type label and health probe:

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth is not limited to chat completions. The same proxy, registry, and billing
pipeline serve embeddings, audio transcription/translation, text-to-speech, and
image generation. Each route declares a `model_type` so obleth knows which
OpenAI endpoint it serves, how to probe it for health, and how to price it.

Every modality stays OpenAI-compatible: point any OpenAI SDK at obleth, change
only the `base_url`, and call the matching endpoint.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Speech-to-text (transcriptions & translations)
chunks.text:
STT clients upload audio as `multipart/form-data`. obleth parses the multipart
body, swaps the `model` field to the route's `upstream_model`, and forwards the
audio file unchanged.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "qwen3-asr",
    "model_type": "audio_transcription",
    "upstream_model": "Qwen/Qwen3-ASR",
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "api_key": "sk_upstream",
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

```python
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost/v1", api_key="sk_...")

with open("speech.wav", "rb") as f:
    result = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="qwen3-asr",
        file=f,
    )
print(result.text)
```

Both `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` are served by an
`audio_transcription` route.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: Text-to-speech
chunks.text:
TTS routes serve `/v1/audio/speech` and return audio bytes.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "qwen3-tts",
    "model_type": "audio_speech",
    "upstream_model": "Qwen/Qwen3-TTS",
    "api_base": "https://provider.example/v1",
    "api_key": "sk_upstream",
    "cost_per_character": 0.000015,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

```python
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost/v1", api_key="sk_...")

audio = client.audio.speech.create(
    model="qwen3-tts",
    voice="alloy",
    input="Hello from obleth.",
)
audio.write_to_file("out.mp3")
```

TTS is billed per character of input text via `cost_per_character`.

chunks.title: Multi-modal Models
chunks.heading: The `api_base` convention
chunks.text:
> **Important:** `api_base` must be the provider **base** URL ending in `/v1`,
> not a full endpoint URL.

obleth preserves the client's request path and appends it to `api_base`. If a
client calls `/v1/embeddings`, obleth forwards to `{api_base}` + the request
path. So:

| `api_base` | Client path | Upstream URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://provider.example/v1` | `/v1/embeddings` | `https://provider.example/v1/embeddings` (correct) |
| `https://provider.example/v1/embeddings` | `/v1/embeddings` | Doubled path (wrong) |

Set `api_base` to the provider base (for example `https://provider.example/v1`)
for every model type. obleth is defensive against the doubled-path case, but the
base-URL convention is the correct way to configure routes.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Authentication
chunks.text:
Every data-plane request except `GET /health` needs a gateway credential: an
API key (`sk_…`) or an [identity token](/docs/guides/identity-tokens). Either
header is accepted:

```
Authorization: Bearer sk_<48 hex chars>
x-api-key: sk_<48 hex chars>
```

Identity tokens are short-lived JWT access tokens from the OIDC issuers
configured in `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS`, sent in the same headers; a verified token
maps to a per-user identity key under the configured tenant.

The admin token (`OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN`) is for the Management API only. Never
send it to the data plane. See [Authentication](/docs/reference/authentication)
for error responses.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Gateway headers
chunks.text:
Headers obleth itself reads or sets. Of the request headers, only
`x-obleth-boons` is stripped before forwarding; the others also reach the
upstream.

| Header | Direction | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-boons` | request | Comma-separated boon controls: `off` skips all boons for the request; `lossy` forces the compression boon's lossy pass (for A/B testing). `off` wins if both are present. |
| `x-obleth-effort` | request | Explicit difficulty (`low`, `medium`, or `high`) for `model: "auto"` routing; wins over the classifier and heuristics. |
| `x-obleth-session-id` / `x-session-id` | request | Session grouping (see [Session tracking](#session-tracking)). |
| `x-obleth-request-id` | response | The gateway's request id, set on every proxied response; quote it when correlating logs and traces. |
| `x-obleth-boons` | response | The boons that were applied, comma-separated. |
| `x-obleth-boons-warning` | response | A boon hit a non-fatal problem, such as a structured-output validation failure where the original completion passed through. |
| `x-obleth-cache` | response | `hit` when the response was served from the response cache. |
| `x-obleth-compression` | response | `before=<tokens>;after=<tokens>;saved=<tokens>` when the compression boon ran. |

The full header reference is in
[Data-plane Routes](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: `GET /model/info`
chunks.text:
The gateway's own description of every enabled route (pricing, capability
flags, context window, quantization, tags, aliases, boons, and last observed
health), filtered by the tenant's allowlist. It is served from the registry,
so a route is listed whether or not its backend is answering, and it never
includes a route's `api_base` or `api_key`. See
[Model Registry](/docs/guides/model-registry#get-modelinfo).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: `GET /v1/models`
chunks.text:
obleth does not forward this to one upstream. It asks every distinct upstream
behind a registered model (each model's endpoints or `api_base`, authenticated
with that model's key) for its own catalog and merges the entries, so models
on separate backends, including Slurm-provisioned ones, appear together.
Lookups are concurrent and best-effort, with a 4-second timeout each; an
upstream that fails is skipped. Each upstream catalog is tried at `/v1/models`
and then `/v1/models/`, which some gateways require. The merged listing is
cached for 15 seconds; a listing with a missing upstream is served but not
cached.

Entries a registered route recognizes (by its `model_name`, an alias, or the
`upstream_model` its backend reports) are rewritten to the route's
`model_name`, listed once, and annotated:

- `model_type`: `chat`, `embedding`, `audio_transcription`, `audio_speech`, or
  `image`
- `mode`: the LiteLLM-convention spelling, identical except `image` is
  `image_generation`
- `quantization`, `tags`, and `aliases`

So a backend that reports `glm-5-3-mxfp4` is listed as the registered
`glm-5-3`. Entries no route claims (wildcard passthroughs) are left as the
upstream reported them. `GET /v1/models/` (trailing slash) returns the same
listing. The listing is returned whatever the request body contains, so a
stale `{"model": …}` left in a reused REST-client request does not turn the
list call into a per-model lookup. The listing is not filtered by the tenant's
model allowlist; callin

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: `GET /v1/models/{id}`
chunks.text:
Answered from the registry for any registered name or alias, with the same
annotations and `owned_by: "obleth"`. An id no route claims is forwarded
upstream.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Headers forwarded to upstream
chunks.text:
obleth forwards the client's headers to the upstream except `host`,
`content-length`, `connection`, `accept-encoding`, the client's
`Authorization` and `x-api-key` credentials, and `x-obleth-boons` (a gateway
directive). Session headers such as `x-session-id` are forwarded like any
other header. When the model or endpoint has an upstream key, obleth sends it
as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: LangChain
chunks.text:
```python
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8088/v1",
    api_key="sk_...",
    model="llama-3-70b",
)
```

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Models
chunks.text:
obleth routes by the `model` field in the request body. A model can be called
by its canonical `model_name` or by any of its `aliases`. An alias resolves in
the same single lookup and is folded to the canonical name before admission,
budgets, the response cache, the tenant allowlist, and the usage ledger, so a
model's usage is never split across spellings. `model: "auto"` hands the choice
to the [auto router](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing).

Register a model:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "llama-3-70b",
    "description": "Llama 3 70B instruct through Aibrix",
    "upstream_model": "meta-llama/Llama-3-70b-instruct",
    "api_base": "http://my-aibrix:8080/v1",
    "input_cost_per_token": 0.0000005,
    "output_cost_per_token": 0.0000015,
    "context_window": 131072,
    "quantization": "fp8",
    "aliases": ["llama-3-70b-fp8"],
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

Set `api_base` to the provider base URL ending in `/v1`
(`https://provider.example/v1`), not a full endpoint URL. obleth appends the
client's request path to it, so a full endpoint such as `.../v1/embeddings`
would double the path. This applies to every model type. Every route field is
described in [Model Registry](/docs/guides/model-registry).

`quantization` records the serving format as a field from a fixed vocabulary
(`fp8`, `mxfp4`, `awq`, `gguf`, and others; see
[Model Registry](/doc

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Non-streaming request
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3-70b",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "What is obleth?"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0.7
  }'
```

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth's data plane speaks the OpenAI HTTP API. Any OpenAI client works with
only a `base_url` change. The same gateway also serves the
[Anthropic Messages API](/docs/guides/anthropic-messages-api) and a native
[Verdicts API](/docs/guides/verdicts).

Use the data-plane URL for your deployment: `http://localhost:8088` for the
Compose host port, `http://localhost` through the HAProxy edge profile, or
`http://localhost:8080` when running the gateway natively.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Python (openai package)
chunks.text:
```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8088/v1",
    api_key="sk_...",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="llama-3-70b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    max_tokens=64,
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Request limits
chunks.text:
| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Request body | 64 MiB |
| `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` body | 32 MiB |
| MCP body | 16 MiB |
| Response cache entry | 512 KiB (larger responses stream through uncached) |

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Responses API
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/responses` is translated to a chat-completions call, run through the
same pipeline (routing, admission, boons, billing), and translated back into a
Responses object, streaming or not. Usage is recorded with request type
`responses`.

- `instructions` becomes a leading system message; `input` (a string or a list
  of `message`, `function_call`, and `function_call_output` items) becomes the
  conversation. Reasoning items in `input` are dropped.
- `max_output_tokens` becomes `max_tokens`, `text.format` becomes
  `response_format`, and `function` tools are converted. Hosted tool types
  (web search and similar) are dropped.
- Reasoning output from the model is returned as `reasoning` items.
- The gateway keeps no conversation state. `store: true`,
  `previous_response_id`, and `background: true` are rejected with 400 and a
  message asking the client to resend the full conversation in `input`.
- The body limit is 32 MiB (400 above it).
- Pipeline errors are returned unchanged, in the OpenAI error envelope.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Session tracking
chunks.text:
To group related requests in **Request Logs**, send a session identifier on
each call. obleth records it on the usage row. Accepted sources, first match
wins:

| Source | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-session-id` header | `x-obleth-session-id: conv-abc123` |
| `x-session-id` header | `x-session-id: conv-abc123` |
| `session_id` in the JSON body | `{"model": "...", "session_id": "conv-abc123", ...}` |
| `metadata.session_id` in the JSON body | `{"metadata": {"session_id": "conv-abc123"}, ...}` |

Values are trimmed and capped at 200 characters. With none present, obleth
derives a stable id from the conversation's opening. The OpenAI `user` field is
not a session source; it identifies an end user, not a conversation. See
[Conversations & Sessions](/docs/guides/conversations-and-sessions).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Streaming (SSE)
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -N http://localhost:8088/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3-70b",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Count to 5"}],
    "max_tokens": 32
  }'
```

obleth streams the upstream's SSE response through and sets
`x-accel-buffering: no` so intermediate proxies do not buffer it. The fairshare
permit is held until the stream closes. The gateway always asks the upstream
for stream usage and removes that extra chunk when the client did not request
it. A stream that ends before its terminal chunk is reported to the client as
an error.

Every response carries an `x-obleth-request-id` header, which is the id used in
Request Logs and trace lookups.

chunks.heading: Supported routes

| `/v1/completions` | POST | Legacy text completions |
| `/v1/responses` | POST | OpenAI Responses API, translated to chat (see [below](#responses-api)) |
| `/v1/embeddings` | POST | `model_type: embedding` |
| `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations` | POST | Multipart upload, `model_type: audio_transcription` |
| `/v1/audio/speech` | POST | `model_type: audio_speech` |
| `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/images/variations` | POST | `model_type: image` |
| `/v1/rerank`, `/v1/reranking` | POST | Passed through to the named model |
| `/v1/moderations` | POST | Passed through to the named model |
| `/v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens` | POST | [Anthropic Messages API](/docs/guides/anthropic-messages-api) |
