chunks.text:
Fairshare now runs one pool per model. A model's pool size is its
`max_in_flight`, or `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` (default `32`) when
unset. `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` (default `1024`) is a total ceiling across
all pools.

- **A pinned ceiling.** If you set `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` or Helm
  `obleth.globalMaxInFlight` yourself (the Compose file shipped before v1.3.0
  used `64`), raise it above the sum of your models' pool sizes. Otherwise the
  ceiling binds before the pools do, and the gateway logs at start-up:
  `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT is below the sum of the enabled models' pool
  sizes`. The current Compose file sets `1024`.
- **Models without `max_in_flight`.** Such a model now admits at most `32`
  concurrent requests per gateway replica. Set `max_in_flight` on any model that
  needs more, or raise the default pool size (Helm
  `obleth.defaultModelMaxInFlight`). The Compose file hardcodes the default, so
  in Compose set it per model.
- **Tenant `max_in_flight`** is now enforced, per model pool. Tenants that carried
  a value are capped by it from this release on.
- **API keys** gain their own fairshare `weight`, defaulting to `100`, so
  existing keys share their tenant evenly.

See [Fairshare Engine](/docs/concepts/fairshare-engine).

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Behaviour changes to review
chunks.text:
These need no action, but they change what operators and clients observe:

- A Redis error while looking up a key returns `503` (`authentication backend
  unavailable`) instead of `401`.
- A request that waits longer than `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default `60`)
  in the fairshare queue returns `503` with `Retry-After: 5`.
- On SIGTERM the gateway drains in-flight requests for up to
  `OBLETH_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS` (default `300`). A Compose `stop` or `restart` can
  therefore take up to 345 seconds while streams finish. See
  [Shutdown & Timeouts](/docs/operations/graceful-shutdown-and-timeouts).
- Failed upstream calls without a usage block are billed at zero, and term
  budgets are reserved at admission and reconciled at completion. Helper calls
  (vision, structured output, tool loops, drafts, image generation) count
  against tenant and key term budgets.
- Deleting or disabling a key, tenant, model, MCP server, or alias returns `502`
  if the Redis eviction fails. Run `POST /api/v1/resync` (Settings → Data →
  Reconcile cache) to rebuild the cached entries from Postgres.
- Dashboard email sign-up is closed; the break-glass admin is seeded from
  `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`. Portal users can disable their
  own keys but cannot re-enable a key an administrator disabled.
- The Helm chart gives the telemetry spill file a writable volume, rolls pods
  when the chart-rendered Secret changes, and renders the PodDisruptionBudget
  only when more than one r

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Docker Compose upgrades
chunks.text:
Set `OBLETH_VERSION` in `deploy/docker/.env` (or pass it inline), check the
required actions above for your `.env`, then pull and recreate:

```bash
# Pull the new images
OBLETH_VERSION=v1.3.0 docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml pull

# Recreate containers (brief downtime)
OBLETH_VERSION=v1.3.0 docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate
```

If you run the `compressor` profile, set `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION=v1.3.0` as
well. Docker Compose does not support zero-downtime rolling upgrades. The old
gateway container drains in-flight requests for up to 345 seconds before it
exits. For production, use Kubernetes.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Edge / unreleased builds
chunks.text:
Every push to `dev` publishes amd64 `:dev` images, and every push to `main`
publishes `:main`. The compression sidecar has no edge image. To track edge on
top of the current chart:

```bash
helm upgrade obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth --version 1.3.0 \
  -n obleth --reset-then-reuse-values --set image.tag=dev --wait
```

`image.tag` does not apply to the compression sidecar, which reads
`compressor.image.tag`; leave that on a release tag. The `image.tag` pin is kept
by later `--reset-then-reuse-values` upgrades, so set it back to empty (or the
release tag) when you return to releases.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth releases are published in lockstep to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR).
A version-matched upgrade is normally a **chart version bump** — the chart pins
its own matching images, so you do not set image tags by hand. Read the required
actions for every release between your current version and the target before
you upgrade.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Preview first
chunks.text:
```bash
helm upgrade obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth --version 1.3.0 \
  -n obleth --reset-then-reuse-values --dry-run | grep 'image:'
```

Confirm the rendered images are the expected `…:v1.3.0` before applying.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Published artifacts
chunks.text:
| Artifact | Reference | Version form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Helm chart (OCI) | `oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth` | `1.3.0` (no `v`) |
| Container images | `ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/{obleth,control-plane,benchmark-backend,obleth-provisioner,obleth-compressor}` | `v1.3.0` (with `v`) |

Release images are multi-architecture (amd64 and arm64). The Slurm provisioner
and the compression sidecar ship as their own images and are off by default
(`provisioner.enabled`, `compressor.enabled`). When enabled, both advance with
the chart like the rest; the provisioner's running build is shown on
Settings → Slurm, so a stale provisioner deployment is visible.

> **Tag convention.** The **chart** version has no prefix (`1.3.0`); the
> **images** are `v`-prefixed (`v1.3.0`). Same release, two forms.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Rollback
chunks.text:
```bash
helm rollback obleth <previous-revision> -n obleth   # e.g. 18
```

Schema migrations are **not** reverted, but because they are additive the older
binary ignores columns it does not read. Rolling back across v1.3.0 also rolls
back the Redis password: the previous chart runs Redis without authentication.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Schema migrations
chunks.text:
Migrations are **automatic and idempotent**. The numbered files under
`schema/postgres/` are embedded in the gateway binary and applied in order on
every startup (`create … if not exists`, `add column … if not exists`),
serialized across replicas by a Postgres advisory lock so concurrent boots cannot
race. Changes are additive (new columns with defaults, new tables), so old and
new pods coexist during the rolling update. Nothing to run by hand.

The ClickHouse schema is applied the same way: tables and columns are created if
absent on each boot, including the permanent `usage_daily` rollup and its
materialized view, which is rebuilt only when its definition changes. The gateway
boots without ClickHouse and applies the schema once it becomes reachable.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Standard upgrade (recommended)
chunks.text:
Pull the published chart and carry your existing release values (secrets,
datastore URLs, registry overrides) forward so only the version changes:

```bash
helm upgrade obleth \
  oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth \
  --version 1.3.0 \
  --namespace obleth \
  --reset-then-reuse-values \
  --wait
```

When upgrading from a release before v1.3.0, add
`--set redis.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16)` once (see
[required action 1](#1-redis-requires-a-password)).

- The chart's image tags (`image.tag`, `compressor.image.tag`) are **empty by
  default** and resolve to `v{appVersion}` at render time, so one chart upgrade
  carries the gateway, control plane, benchmark backend, provisioner, and
  compressor to the release together.
- `--reset-then-reuse-values` (Helm 3.14+) starts from the **new** chart's
  defaults, then re-applies only the overrides you explicitly set on the previous
  release. Your secrets and overrides are preserved, and values added in the new
  chart version take their defaults.
- `--wait` blocks until the new pods pass their health checks and reports
  failure (without serving traffic from a broken pod) if they don't.

> **Plain `--reuse-values`.** `--reuse-values` reuses the last release's computed
> values and ignores the new chart's defaults, so values introduced by the new
> chart are not filled in. It still renders the new images, because the default
> tag is empty. Prefer `--reset-then-reuse-values` for version bumps.

> **If you pinned `image.tag` e

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Switching an existing release to GHCR
chunks.text:
If a release was originally installed with a private registry override
(`image.obleth`, `image.tag`, …), value reuse keeps that registry. To move it
back onto the public GHCR images, override the image block explicitly once:

```bash
helm upgrade obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth --version 1.3.0 \
  -n obleth --reset-then-reuse-values \
  --set image.obleth=ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/obleth \
  --set image.controlPlane=ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/control-plane \
  --set image.benchmarkBackend=ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/benchmark-backend \
  --set image.provisioner=ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/obleth-provisioner \
  --set image.tag=v1.3.0 \
  --wait
```

Subsequent `--reset-then-reuse-values` upgrades then stay on GHCR.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Upgrading from earlier releases
chunks.text:
- **v0.9.4: `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_RESTART_AFTER_FAILURES`.** The default is `20`
  (about 5 minutes of sustained probe failure at the default tick interval).
  Before v0.9.4 the Compose fallback, the Helm chart default, and `.env.example`
  pinned it to `3`, which cancelled healthy replicas after about 45 seconds of
  probe flapping and resubmitted them in a loop. If you set `3` yourself, remove
  or raise it.
- **v0.5.0: email sign-in for the dashboard.** The dashboard signs in with an
  email address, not a username; the old `DASHBOARD_USERNAME` setting is no
  longer read and can be deleted. Before starting the upgraded control plane:
  1. Set `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` to a real email address. A bare value such as
     `admin` fails validation.
  2. Make sure `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` is at least 8 characters. A shorter password
     is logged as an error and no account is created.
  3. Start the control plane. The break-glass admin is seeded from those values
     only when no active admin exists yet, and never over an existing account
     with the same email.
  4. Sign in with that email and password.

  If either value is wrong, the admin is not created and you are locked out of
  the dashboard until you fix it and restart. SSO users are unaffected; they sign
  in through their provider and wait for approval as before.
- **v0.3.1: Slurm replica endpoints register at the `/v1` root.** Promotion only
  creates an endpoint; it never rewrites an existing one. A replica promoted by

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Upgrading to v1.0.0
chunks.text:
- **Compose binds management ports to localhost.** The Compose stack publishes
  the Management API (`9180`), metrics (`9091`), Prometheus, and Jaeger on
  `127.0.0.1` only. If you reached any of them from another machine, add your own
  port mapping in a Compose override file or route through the edge proxy. The
  data plane, dashboard, and edge proxy ports are unchanged, and Kubernetes
  deployments are unaffected. See
  [Endpoints and Ports](/docs/reference/endpoints-and-ports).
- **Identity tokens are off by default.** Nothing changes until you set
  `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` (Compose) or `obleth.jwtIssuers` (Helm). Migration 0016
  adds the identity columns to `api_keys` on boot. See
  [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens).
- **`DASHBOARD_PASSWORD_HASH` was removed.** The variable was listed in the
  example environment files but never read; the break-glass password has always
  come from `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`. Remove it if you set it.
- **One gateway replica by default.** The chart defaults to
  `obleth.replicas: 1` with the HPA off, because the in-flight ceiling and the
  model pools are enforced per replica. See
  [Scaling](/docs/operations/scaling).

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Upgrading to v1.2.0 and v1.1.0
chunks.text:
- **The edge image tag is `:dev`.** Features integrate on `dev` and are promoted
  to `main` at release. `:dev` is the moving edge tag; `:main` tracks
  release-ready work. If you tested unreleased fixes with `OBLETH_VERSION=main`,
  move to `dev`.
- **The compression sidecar has its own tag.** Compose reads
  `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` (default `latest`) for the `obleth-compressor`
  image, because edge builds do not publish that image. Set it and
  `OBLETH_VERSION` to the same `vX.Y.Z` to pin a release.
- **The model manifest replaces the dashboard template importer.** Export and
  import the model registry as an `obleth-models` manifest. See
  [Model Registry](/docs/guides/model-registry).

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Verify
chunks.text:
```bash
helm history obleth -n obleth | tail -2

kubectl -n obleth get deploy -o \
  'jsonpath={range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}'

kubectl -n obleth get pods
```

The gateway log should show `postgres connected + schema applied`,
`redis connected`, `clickhouse connected + schema applied`, and
`listening: proxy=…`:

```bash
kubectl -n obleth logs deploy/obleth-obleth -c obleth --tail=25
```

If ClickHouse is unreachable at boot, the log shows `telemetry started in spill
mode` instead, and usage rows spill to the local file until it returns.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Authentication failures
chunks.text:
| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No credential | `401` | `missing bearer token` |
| Unknown API key, or a deleted key | `401` | `invalid api key` |
| JWT failed verification | `401` | `invalid token` |
| Redis (or the identity backend) failed during the lookup | `503` | `authentication backend unavailable` |
| Verified JWT that could not be mapped to an identity key | `503` | `identity provisioning unavailable` |
| Key disabled | `403` | `api key disabled` |
| Tenant not active, not yet active, expired, or outside its schedule | `403` | See [Data Plane Routes](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes#authentication) |

A Redis error during the key lookup returns `503`, never `401`, so a Redis
outage does not look like a revoked key. `/v1/messages` returns the same
conditions in the Anthropic error envelope, with `missing api key` when no
credential is sent.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Creating a key
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants/$TENANT_ID/keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "batch-jobs", "weight": 50, "max_in_flight": 8}'
```

The response carries the key record and, once only, the secret:

```json
{
  "key": {
    "id": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222",
    "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
    "name": "batch-jobs",
    "key_prefix": "sk_a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b",
    "kind": "secret",
    "weight": 50,
    "max_in_flight": 8,
    "disabled": false
  },
  "secret": "sk_a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2..."
}
```

`weight` (default `100`, minimum `1`) sets the key's share of its tenant's
capacity relative to the tenant's other keys; `max_in_flight` (default `null`,
uncapped) caps the key's concurrent requests within each model pool. The full
record and every body field are in the
[Management API reference](/docs/reference/management-api#api-keys).

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Dashboard
chunks.text:
The control-plane dashboard has its own sign-in, separate from the Management
API. Accounts and sessions are stored in the
[dashboard auth tables](/docs/reference/postgres-schema#dashboard-auth-tables)
in Postgres, sessions are signed with `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (which defaults to
`DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET`), and sign-in is accepted only from `BETTER_AUTH_URL`
and `TRUSTED_ORIGINS`. Single sign-on is configured with `OIDC_PROVIDERS`; see
[Dashboard SSO](/docs/guides/dashboard-sso). The dashboard server calls the
Management API with `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN`; the token never reaches the browser.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Data plane
chunks.text:
Every data-plane request except `GET /health` carries a tenant credential:

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk_<48 hex chars>
```

The gateway also accepts the credential in the `x-api-key` header, which it
reads when no `Authorization: Bearer` header is present. Anthropic SDKs send
that header by default.

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_a1b2c3d4e5f6..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "example-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

A credential that starts with `eyJ`, contains exactly two dots, and is at most
8 KiB is verified as a JWT access token when `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is set.
Everything else is looked up as an API key. Token verification is off unless
`OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is set. See [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens).

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Hash pepper
chunks.text:
When `OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER` is set, it is mixed into the key hash, so a leaked
database alone cannot be used to confirm guessed keys. When it is unset, hashing
is plain SHA-256 of the secret. Adding, changing, or removing the pepper
invalidates every previously issued secret key; those keys must be reissued.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Identity tokens (JWT)
chunks.text:
When `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is set, the data plane accepts short-lived JWT access
tokens from trusted OIDC issuers alongside API keys. Setup and the issuer-side
steps are in [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens).

A token is verified offline against the issuer's cached JWKS signing keys. The
key set is refreshed in the background every 15 minutes; a token whose `kid` is
not in the cache triggers a refetch, limited to one per issuer per minute.
Verification allows 60 seconds of clock skew. A verified token maps to an
identity key: an `api_keys` row with `kind = 'identity'` whose `key_hash` is
`jwt:` followed by the SHA-256 of the issuer, a zero byte, and the subject. The
row is created on the first verified token for that subject. From then on the
request is handled exactly like one authenticated with a secret key: tenant
status, schedules, budgets, model allowlists, and disable all apply. The
dashboard Keys page marks these keys with an `identity` badge.

`OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is a JSON array read once at startup. A parse error stops
the gateway from starting rather than silently disabling an issuer. Each entry
takes:

| Field | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `issuer` | yes | | Exact match on the token's `iss` claim. |
| `audience` | yes | | Exact match on the token's `aud` claim. |
| `tenant` | yes | | Tenant that identity keys for this issuer are created under. |
| `jwks_url` | no | `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json` | Where the signing keys

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Key format
chunks.text:
| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Prefix | `sk_` |
| Secret part | 48 hex characters (24 random bytes) |
| Total length | 51 characters |
| Display prefix (`key_prefix`) | First 18 characters |

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Key kinds
chunks.text:
| `kind` | Credential | Created by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | `sk_…` secret, shown once | Dashboard or Management API |
| `identity` | None; the caller presents an identity token | The gateway, on the first verified token for a subject |

An identity key has no secret to present, copy, or rotate. Its `key_hash` holds a
deterministic handle derived from the issuer and subject rather than a hashed
secret, and its lifecycle control is disable, not delete. Tenant, weight,
budget, model allowlist, and usage rows behave as they do for a secret key.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Key lifecycle
chunks.text:
| Action | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Create | `POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/keys` |
| List all keys | `GET /api/v1/keys` |
| List one tenant's keys | `GET /api/v1/keys?tenant_id={id}` |
| Replace name, description, budget, `weight`, and `max_in_flight` | `PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}` |
| Disable or re-enable | `PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}/disabled` with `{"disabled": true}` or `false` |
| Enable or disable span tracing | `PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}/tracing` |
| Delete | `DELETE /api/v1/keys/{id}` |

A disabled key returns `403` `api key disabled`. A deleted key returns `401`
`invalid api key`.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Key storage
chunks.text:
obleth never stores the raw key. On creation the gateway:

1. Generates 24 cryptographically random bytes.
2. Hex-encodes them and prepends `sk_`.
3. Computes the key hash: SHA-256 over the full secret, followed by a zero byte
   and the pepper when `OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER` is set.
4. Stores the hash and display prefix in Postgres (`api_keys.key_hash`,
   `api_keys.key_prefix`) and writes the resolved key to Redis under
   `obleth:key:<hash>`.
5. Returns the full secret once.

On each request the gateway hashes the presented key and looks the hash up in
its in-process cache (entries live up to 300 seconds and are dropped early by
[invalidation messages](/docs/reference/redis-layout#invalidation-channel)),
then in Redis. The data plane never reads Postgres on the request path. Redis is
written by the Management API on every change and rebuilt from Postgres when a
gateway process starts, periodically, and after a Redis reconnect. See
[Redis Layout](/docs/reference/redis-layout#rebuilding-from-postgres).

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Management API
chunks.text:
Every Management API request (port `9180`) carries the admin token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN>
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

`OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` has no default; the gateway refuses to start without it.
The presented header is compared with the expected value in constant time. A
missing or wrong token returns `401` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`. There is
no per-user role model on the Management API: the token grants full access.
Protect it as described in [Security](/docs/operations/security).

Three routes need no token: `GET /api/v1/health`, `GET /api/v1/version`, and
`GET /api/v1/openapi.json`.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Admission class distribution
chunks.text:
```sql
SELECT
    admission,
    count() AS requests,
    round(count() / sum(count()) OVER () * 100, 1) AS pct
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) * 1000
GROUP BY admission;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Cache hit rate by model
chunks.text:
```sql
SELECT
    model,
    countIf(cache_status = 'hit')  AS hits,
    countIf(cache_status = 'miss') AS misses,
    round(countIf(cache_status = 'hit') / count() * 100, 1) AS hit_pct
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) * 1000
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY hits DESC;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Cost by tenant
chunks.text:
Each request stores its USD cost frozen at completion time, so spend is a plain
`sum` — no join against the pricing table and no read-time multiply:

```sql
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    sum(cost_usd) AS total_cost_usd
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY) * 1000
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```

The Management API `/api/v1/costs` endpoint returns this per model, and
`/api/v1/usage/daily` exposes `cost_usd` at any `group_by` (including
`key_model` for per-key, per-model spend). For long ranges, sum `cost_usd_sum`
from the permanent `usage_daily` rollup below instead of the raw ledger.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Data retention
chunks.text:
obleth prunes the raw `usage` ledger automatically. A background worker runs
hourly and drops whole day-partitions older than the retention window — an O(1)
metadata operation rather than a row delete. The window defaults to
`OBLETH_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (180) and is tunable live from the control plane
via `PUT /api/v1/settings/usage-retention`, accepting 1 to 36500 days; a stored value outside that range is clamped, so a
misconfigured value can never wipe the whole ledger. The `usage_daily` rollup
is never touched by retention.

To prune on demand instead of waiting for the worker, call
`POST /api/v1/usage/compact`. You do **not** need to add a manual ClickHouse
`TTL` — retention is handled by the gateway.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Last used per key
chunks.text:
The dashboard Keys table and
[`GET /api/v1/keys/{id}/usage`](/docs/reference/management-api#per-key-usage-summary)
report when each key was last seen and what it last called. `argMax` reads the
most recent row's value without a self-join:

```sql
SELECT
    key_id,
    max(ts_ms)                 AS last_used_ms,
    argMax(model, ts_ms)       AS last_model,
    argMax(status_code, ts_ms) AS last_status_code,
    count()                    AS requests,
    sum(cost_usd)              AS cost_usd
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY) * 1000
GROUP BY key_id
ORDER BY requests DESC;
```

The single-key endpoint filters by `key_id` and drops the `ts_ms` floor on
`last_used_ms` (it stays accurate across the full retention window), applying the
window only to the `count`/`sum` columns via `countIf` / `sumIf`.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
ClickHouse stores the append-only usage ledger. The gateway inserts rows and
never updates them; the only deletion is the retention worker dropping whole day
partitions of the raw ledger.

The gateway creates its tables at startup, and adds missing columns and indexes
idempotently, in the database named by `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_DB` (default
`obleth`):

| Table | Engine | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | `MergeTree` | One row per request, pruned to the retention window |
| `usage_daily` | `SummingMergeTree` | Permanent daily rollup of `usage`, never pruned |
| `usage_daily_mv` | Materialized view | Feeds `usage_daily` from new `usage` inserts |
| `usage_meta` | `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)` | Internal markers, such as the one-time rollup backfill flag |
| `spans` | `MergeTree` | Per-request timing spans, kept 14 days |

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: P50/P95/P99 latency
chunks.text:
```sql
SELECT
    quantile(0.50)(ttft_ms) AS p50_ttft_ms,
    quantile(0.95)(ttft_ms) AS p95_ttft_ms,
    quantile(0.99)(ttft_ms) AS p99_ttft_ms,
    quantile(0.50)(total_ms) AS p50_total_ms,
    quantile(0.95)(total_ms) AS p95_total_ms
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) * 1000;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Recent requests (newest first)
chunks.text:
The dashboard **Request Logs** page and
[`GET /api/v1/usage/logs`](/docs/reference/management-api#request-logs) read
individual rows from this table. This is the only Management API usage endpoint
that returns per-request detail rather than an aggregate:

```sql
SELECT
    request_id,
    ts_ms,
    tenant_id,
    key_id,
    model,
    request_type,
    session_id,
    status_code,
    input_tokens + output_tokens AS total_tokens,
    ttft_ms,
    total_ms,
    cost_usd
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) * 1000
ORDER BY ts_ms DESC, toString(request_id) DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Request types
chunks.text:
`request_type` records the class of each row. It powers the **Type** column in
the dashboard **Request Logs** view and the `request_type` filter on
[`GET /api/v1/usage/logs`](/docs/reference/management-api#request-logs).

Client requests are classified by the path suffix, except that the two
translated surfaces are recorded under their own name:

| Value | Written for |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | `/v1/chat/completions` |
| `completion` | `/v1/completions` |
| `responses` | `/v1/responses` |
| `messages` | `/v1/messages` |
| `verdict` | `/v1/verdicts` |
| `embedding` | `/v1/embeddings` |
| `audio` | Any path under `/v1/audio/` |
| `image` | Any path under `/v1/images/` |
| `rerank` | `/v1/rerank` and `/v1/reranking` |
| `moderation` | `/v1/moderations` |
| `other` | Any other forwarded path |

A [verdicts](/docs/guides/verdicts) request writes one `verdict` row whose
tokens and cost are the sum of its per-question single-token calls. The
individual questions appear only as `verdict:q:<id>` spans, not as ledger rows.

Calls the gateway makes to a helper model on a request's behalf are recorded as
their own rows, one row per helper call, with admission `boon` and the tokens
and cost of that call:

| Value | Written for |
| --- | --- |
| `vision_boon` | Image descriptions made by the vision boon's describer model |
| `structured_output_boon` | Structured-output repair calls |
| `tool_loop` | Each round trip of the gateway-run MCP tool loop |
| `guardrails_boon` | [Guardrails](/docs

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: `spans` table
chunks.text:
```sql
CREATE TABLE obleth.spans (
    request_id        UUID,
    span_name         LowCardinality(String),
    parent_span       String DEFAULT '',
    start_ms          Int64,
    duration_ms       UInt32,
    status            LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT 'ok',
    attributes        String DEFAULT '',
    session_id        String DEFAULT '',
    session_id_source LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT ''
) ENGINE = MergeTree()
  PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(start_ms))
  ORDER BY (request_id, start_ms)
  TTL toDate(fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(start_ms)) + INTERVAL 14 DAY DELETE;
```

`spans` holds the per-request timing breakdown returned by the request spans
endpoint of the [Management API](/docs/reference/management-api#request-spans).
Unlike `usage`, it is expired by a ClickHouse `TTL` after 14 days rather than by
the retention worker. Spans are written only for requests whose key or tenant has
tracing enabled (`PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}/tracing` or
`PUT /api/v1/tenants/{id}/tracing`). `session_id` and `session_id_source`
mirror the usage row, so spans can be grouped by conversation.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Token usage by tenant (last 24h)
chunks.text:
```sql
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    sum(input_tokens)  AS input_tokens,
    sum(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
    count()            AS requests
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= (now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) * 1000
  AND request_type NOT IN ('health_probe', 'benchmark')
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY output_tokens DESC;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: `usage_daily` rollup
chunks.text:
The raw `usage` ledger is pruned on a retention window to bound storage, so
long-range reporting reads from a permanent daily rollup instead. `usage_daily`
holds one row per `day × tenant × key × model` and is **never** pruned, so
historical totals survive indefinitely.

```sql
CREATE TABLE obleth.usage_daily (
    day              Date,
    tenant_id        UUID,
    key_id           UUID,
    model            String,
    requests         UInt64,
    success_requests UInt64,   -- status_code 2xx/3xx
    error_requests   UInt64,   -- status_code >= 400
    input_tokens     UInt64,
    output_tokens    UInt64,
    estimated_tokens UInt64,
    cache_hits       UInt64,
    cache_misses     UInt64,
    ttft_ms_sum      UInt64,   -- summed over successful requests only
    total_ms_sum     UInt64,   -- summed over successful requests only
    cost_usd_sum     Float64,  -- summed USD cost (frozen at request time)
    energy_wh_sum    Float64,  -- summed attributed watt-hours
    energy_cost_usd_sum Float64, -- summed energy cost (USD)
    co2_g_sum        Float64   -- summed grams CO₂
) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree()
  PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(day)
  ORDER BY (day, tenant_id, key_id, model);
```

A materialized view (`usage_daily_mv`) keeps the rollup current as new requests
land, and a one-time guarded backfill seeds it from any history that predates
the view. The backfill runs only when the rollup is empty, so a restart can
never double-count. `SummingMergeTree` collapses rows sharing

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: `usage_meta` table
chunks.text:
`usage_meta` (`key`, `value`, `updated_at`; `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)`
ordered by `(key, value)`) stores internal markers, such as the flag recording
that the one-time `usage_daily` backfill has run. It holds no usage data.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: `usage` table
chunks.text:
```sql
CREATE TABLE obleth.usage (
    request_id       UUID,
    tenant_id        UUID,
    key_id           UUID,
    model            String,
    admission        LowCardinality(String), -- 'fast' | 'queued' | 'rejected' | 'boon' | 'health_probe'
    weight           Int64,        -- tenant weight at time of request
    input_tokens     UInt32,
    output_tokens    UInt32,
    estimated_tokens UInt32,       -- pre-request estimate used for budgeting
    queue_wait_ms    UInt32,
    ttft_ms          UInt32,       -- time to first token
    total_ms         UInt32,       -- total request duration
    status_code      UInt16,
    cache_status     LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT 'off', -- 'hit' | 'miss' | 'off'
    cost_usd         Float64 DEFAULT 0, -- USD cost frozen at request completion
    energy_wh        Float64 DEFAULT 0, -- attributed watt-hours (energy accounting)
    energy_cost_usd  Float64 DEFAULT 0, -- energy priced at the configured $/kWh
    co2_g            Float64 DEFAULT 0, -- grams CO₂ at the configured grid intensity
    ts_ms            Int64,        -- Unix timestamp milliseconds
    session_id       String DEFAULT '', -- client session/conversation id (optional)
    session_id_source LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT '', -- how session_id was obtained
    request_type     LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT '', -- see Request types below
    device_id        String DEFAULT '', -- device claim from an identity token
    ts               DateTime64(3) MATERIALIZED

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: Useful queries
chunks.text:
Every example below reads all traffic. To match what the Management API and the
dashboard report by default, add
`AND request_type NOT IN ('health_probe', 'benchmark')`.

chunks.title: ClickHouse Usage Schema
chunks.heading: WAL and replay
chunks.text:
When ClickHouse is unavailable after startup, obleth spills rows to a WAL file
(`OBLETH_WAL_PATH`). On reconnect the spill segments are replayed in order, in
checkpointed batches with retry backoff, so a large backlog is drained with
bounded memory. New spill stops at 256 MiB or 1,024 files; past that, records are
dropped and counted in the `obleth_telemetry_dropped` gauge. Rows in the WAL have
the same structure as `usage`.

Each batch is inserted with an `insert_deduplication_token` derived from the
request IDs it contains, and both `usage` and `usage_daily` carry
`non_replicated_deduplication_window = 10000`. A batch whose insert timed out
after ClickHouse had already committed it is replayed from the WAL with the same
token, and ClickHouse discards the duplicate, so replay does not double-count
the ledger or the rollup.

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Anthropic Messages API
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/messages` is translated to a chat-completions request. All system
text, from the top-level `system` field and from any system-role entries, is
placed at the front of the conversation. The `anthropic-beta` header and the
`beta` query parameter are not forwarded upstream. Errors use the Anthropic
envelope:

```json
{ "type": "error", "error": { "type": "not_found_error", "message": "model: example-model" } }
```

| Status | `error.type` |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` |
| `401` | `authentication_error` |
| `403` | `permission_error` |
| `404` | `not_found_error` |
| `413` | `request_too_large` |
| `429` | `rate_limit_error` |
| `502`, `503`, `504` | `overloaded_error` |

The body limit is 32 MiB; a larger body returns `413`. A missing credential
returns `401` `missing api key`. An unknown model is served by the configured
default model for Anthropic clients (`messages_default_model`) when one is set,
and otherwise returns `404`. The ledger records these requests as
`request_type = messages`.

`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` returns `{"input_tokens": <n>}`, the gateway's
own estimate of the translated prompt. It is not admitted, not budgeted, and
not recorded in the usage ledger.

See [Anthropic Messages API](/docs/guides/anthropic-messages-api).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Authentication
chunks.text:
The credential is read from `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, or from the
`x-api-key` header when no bearer token is present. It is either an API key
(`sk_` followed by 48 hex characters) or, when identity tokens are configured,
a JWT. See [Authentication](/docs/reference/authentication).

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No credential | `401` | `missing bearer token` |
| Unknown API key | `401` | `invalid api key` |
| JWT rejected | `401` | `invalid token` |
| Redis or identity backend unreachable | `503` | `authentication backend unavailable` |
| Verified JWT that cannot be mapped to a key | `503` | `identity provisioning unavailable` |
| Key disabled | `403` | `api key disabled` |
| Tenant not active | `403` | `tenant is not active` |
| Before the tenant's activation time | `403` | `tenant is not active yet` |
| After the tenant's expiry | `403` | `tenant access has expired` |
| Outside the tenant's weekly schedule | `403` | `tenant is outside its scheduled access window` |

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Error responses
chunks.text:
Gateway errors on the OpenAI-compatible routes use this body:

```json
{ "error": { "message": "token budget exceeded", "type": "obleth_gateway_error" } }
```

| Status | Message | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid request path` | Path traversal in the request path |
| `400` | `invalid JSON body` | Body is not valid JSON (Responses, verdicts) |
| `403` | `api key term budget exhausted` | The key's term budget is spent |
| `403` | `tenant term budget exhausted` | The tenant's term budget is spent |
| `413` | `request body too large` | Body over 64 MiB |
| `429` | `token budget exceeded` | Per-minute token budget exhausted |
| `502` | `upstream request failed` | Every endpoint and attempt failed |
| `502` | `upstream response too large` | A translated surface's upstream response exceeded its buffer |
| `503` | `timed out waiting for model capacity` | No slot opened within the admission timeout; carries `Retry-After: 5` |
| `503` | `scheduler unavailable` | The fairshare scheduler could not admit the request |
| `503` | `budget check failed`, `key budget check failed` | Redis failed during the budget reservation |
| `504` | `upstream request timed out` | The final attempt hit the upstream timeout |

Errors returned by an upstream are passed through with the upstream's status and
body.

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Header handling
chunks.text:
obleth forwards client headers upstream except these:

- `host`
- `content-length`
- `connection`
- `accept-encoding`
- `authorization` (replaced by the endpoint's or model's `api_key` when set)
- `x-api-key`
- `x-obleth-boons` (a gateway directive; see [Model Boons](/docs/guides/model-boons))

Session headers such as `x-obleth-session-id` and `x-session-id` are forwarded.

Gateway request headers:

| Header | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-boons` | Per-request boon directive |
| `x-obleth-session-id` | Conversation id for the usage ledger; see [Conversations & Sessions](/docs/guides/conversations-and-sessions) |
| `x-obleth-effort` | Effort hint for [`auto` routing](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing) |

Gateway response headers:

| Header | Present when |
| --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-request-id` | Always on proxied requests; the id to use with [`GET /api/v1/usage/logs`](/docs/reference/management-api#request-logs) |
| `x-obleth-cache: hit` | The response came from the response cache |
| `x-obleth-compression` | The compression boon ran: `before=<tokens>;after=<tokens>;saved=<tokens>` |
| `x-obleth-boons-warning` | A boon hit a non-fatal problem, such as a structured-output validation failure where the original completion passed through |

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: MCP gateway
chunks.text:
Registered MCP servers are reachable at `/mcp/{server}` and any sub-path, with
the same credential as the data plane. obleth authenticates the credential,
applies the same key and tenant checks, resolves the server, replaces
`Authorization` with the server's stored `auth_header`, and reverse-proxies the
request and response bodies unchanged. It does not parse JSON-RPC, so both
streamable-HTTP and SSE transports work. Request bodies are capped at 16 MiB.

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path traversal in the sub-path | `400` | `invalid request path` |
| No credential, or invalid credential | `401` | as in [Authentication](#authentication) |
| Key disabled or tenant not active | `403` | as in [Authentication](#authentication) |
| Server disabled | `403` | `mcp server is disabled` |
| Server not registered | `404` | `mcp server '<name>' is not registered` |
| Body over 16 MiB | `413` | `request body too large` |
| Upstream unreachable | `502` | `mcp upstream request failed` |

Outcomes are counted in
[`obleth_mcp_requests_total`](/docs/reference/prometheus-metrics#obleth_mcp_requests_total).
See [MCP Gateway](/docs/guides/mcp-gateway).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Model discovery
chunks.text:
`GET /v1/models` (with or without a trailing slash) fetches `/v1/models` from
every distinct upstream base in the registry (the default base plus each
model's endpoints), with each base's stored API key and a 4-second timeout per
upstream, and returns the merged list. The first upstream to report an id wins.
An entry that matches a registered model is rewritten to the registered
`model_name`, listed once even when the backend knows it only by its quantized
name, and annotated with `quantization`, `tags`, and `aliases`; other entries
are returned as the upstream reported them. The listing is cached for 15
seconds. A listing that is missing an unreachable upstream is returned but not
cached. A request body on this call is ignored.

`GET /v1/models/{id}` answers from the registry for any registered name or
alias, with `owned_by: "obleth"`. An id no model claims is forwarded upstream,
so a wildcard passthrough keeps working. Neither `/v1/models` route is filtered
by the tenant's model allowlist.

`GET /model/info` and `GET /v1/model/info` are answered from the registry, not
the backends, and list every enabled registered model the tenant is allowed to
call, whether or not its backend is reachable. The body has the form
`{"data": [{"model_name": …, "obleth_params": …, "model_info": …}]}`.
`obleth_params` carries the upstream `model` name and never includes `api_base`
or `api_key`. `model_info` carries the conventional keys (`mode`,
`max_input_tokens`, `*_cost_per_token`, `supports

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Multipart uploads
chunks.text:
For audio transcription and translation, obleth parses the
`multipart/form-data` body, replaces the `model` field with the route's
`upstream_model`, rebuilds the form, and forwards the file part unchanged. A
malformed body returns `400` `invalid multipart body` or
`invalid multipart boundary`.

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The data plane listens on `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN` (default `0.0.0.0:8080`) and
proxies OpenAI-compatible requests to the registered upstreams. Every route
except `/health` requires a credential.

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Registered-model paths
chunks.text:
These paths resolve the request `model` field (or the multipart `model` field
for audio uploads) against the model registry, including aliases:
`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/responses`,
`/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, `/v1/audio/speech`, and
the three `/v1/images/*` paths.

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No `model` | `400` | `model is required` |
| Unregistered name | `404` | `model '<name>' is not registered` |
| Model disabled | `403` | `model is disabled` |
| Tenant allowlist excludes the model | `403` | `model not permitted for tenant` |
| `model: "auto"` with no eligible model | `503` | `no model is available to satisfy the auto request` |

An alias is replaced by the model's canonical name before admission, budgets,
caching, the allowlist check, and the usage ledger. Only chat routes take part
in [`auto` routing](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing).
`/v1/verdicts` resolves `model` the same way, including aliases and `auto`; see
[Verdicts](#verdicts).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Request handling
chunks.text:
1. The credential resolves to a key and tenant; disabled keys and inactive or
   out-of-schedule tenants are rejected.
2. The body is read (up to 64 MiB) and the model is resolved against the
   registry.
3. Model boons that rewrite the request run.
4. When the model has caching enabled, the [response cache](#response-cache) is
   checked. A hit returns immediately.
5. Admission: the request takes a slot in the model's pool or waits for one, up
   to `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS`.
6. The per-minute token budget and any term budgets are reserved atomically in
   Redis.
7. The request is forwarded with the selected endpoint's (or the model's)
   `api_key` in `Authorization`, bounded by the upstream timeout, retried on
   transient failures, and failed over to the next endpoint when configured.
8. The response is streamed back. Token counts are read from the upstream's
   usage report when present.
9. The reservation is reconciled with actual usage, and a usage row is written
   to ClickHouse, or to the write-ahead log when ClickHouse is unavailable.

A request that fails upstream after all attempts is not billed: the per-minute
reservation is refunded and any term reservation released.

For non-token modalities, cost is computed from the response shape: image
routes bill `n × cost_per_image`, and text-to-speech bills input characters ×
`cost_per_character`. Embeddings bill prompt tokens at `input_cost_per_token`.
See [Multi-modal Models](/docs/guides/multi-modal-models).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Response cache
chunks.text:
When caching is enabled for a model and its `cache_ttl_secs` is greater than 0,
the data plane:

1. Computes SHA-256 over the tenant id, a zero byte, the model name, a zero
   byte, and the request body.
2. Looks up `obleth:cache:<hash>` in Redis.
3. On a hit, returns the stored response with `x-obleth-cache: hit`, before
   admission and budget reservation, with no upstream call.
4. On a miss, forwards the request and stores a successful `200` response of up
   to 512 KiB for `cache_ttl_secs`.

Caching is skipped for requests that run the gateway tool loop or output
guardrails. The usage ledger records `cache_status` as `hit`, `miss`, or `off`.
See [Response Cache](/docs/guides/response-cache).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Responses API
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/responses` is translated to a chat-completions request and served by a
registered chat model. The body limit is 32 MiB; a larger or unreadable body
returns `400` `request body too large or unreadable`. Errors use the OpenAI
envelope above, including `401` `missing bearer token`. A request that sets
`store: true`, `background: true`, or a non-null `previous_response_id` returns `400`, because the
gateway keeps no server-side response state.

Input items, `instructions`, `max_output_tokens`, `text.format` (mapped to
`response_format`), and tools are carried across. Streaming responses are
re-emitted as Responses events with contiguous sequence numbers, and a reasoning
model's scratchpad is returned as `reasoning` output items. Translated requests
run the full chat pipeline (routing, fairshare, boons), and the usage ledger
records them as `request_type = responses`. See
[OpenAI-compatible API](/docs/guides/openai-compatible-api).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Route table
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Handling |

| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness check, no credential; returns plain `ok` |
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat completions, streaming and non-streaming |

| `POST` | `/v1/embeddings` | Embeddings |
| `POST` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | Speech-to-text, `multipart/form-data` |

| `GET` | `/v1/models/{id}` | Registry entry for a registered name or alias; otherwise forwarded upstream |
| `GET` | `/model/info`, `/v1/model/info` | Registry d

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Upstream URL construction
chunks.text:
obleth appends the request path to the selected endpoint's `api_base` (or the
model's `api_base`). Configure `api_base` as the provider base ending in `/v1`,
not a full endpoint URL, to avoid a doubled path such as
`.../v1/embeddings/v1/embeddings`. See
[Reliability & Failover](/docs/guides/reliability-and-failover).

chunks.title: Data Plane Routes
chunks.heading: Verdicts
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/verdicts` evaluates a `state` (a string, object, or array) against a
map of typed questions (`boolean`, `choice` with 2 to 26 options, or `score`
with 2 to 10 levels) and returns one verdict per question with a probability
distribution and a confidence. No text is generated. Each question is one
single-token call to the route's chat backend (`max_tokens: 1` with
`top_logprobs`), and the first-token distribution over the answer labels is the
answer. The questions run concurrently against one pinned endpoint and share a
byte-identical prompt prefix, so additional questions mostly hit the backend's
prefix cache.

`model` accepts any registered `chat` model or `auto`. For reasoning models the
gateway retries past the scratchpad: `<think>`-style models with an empty
think-block prefill, and harmony-channel models (such as gpt-oss) with a prompt
splice sent to `/v1/completions`. The variant that worked is remembered per
model. One fairshare permit and one budget reservation cover all questions; the
usage ledger records one row with `request_type = 'verdict'`, and the trace has
one `verdict:q:<id>` span per question. The [Verdicts guide](/docs/guides/verdicts)
covers the request shape, the confidence formula, and limits.

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Compression sidecar
chunks.text:
`COMPRESSOR_CPUS` (default `4`) sets both the container CPU quota and the
onnxruntime thread count. The scoring model is chosen at build time with
`COMPRESSOR_SOURCE` (`onnx`), `COMPRESSOR_MODEL_ID`
(`chopratejas/kompress-v2-base`), and `COMPRESSOR_ONNX_FILE`
(`onnx/kompress-fp32.onnx`). The gateway uses the sidecar only when
`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL=http://compressor:8080` is set, and fails open when it is
unreachable.

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The Compose stack lives in `deploy/docker/` and is the quickest way to run obleth
on one host for development, evaluation, or staging. Run every command from that
directory so Compose loads `deploy/docker/.env`.

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Required variables
chunks.text:
Compose refuses to start when any of these is unset or empty:

| Variable | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `postgres`, and composed into `OBLETH_DATABASE_URL` and the dashboard's `DATABASE_URL` |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | `redis` (`--requirepass`), `redis-exporter`, and composed into `OBLETH_REDIS_URL` as `redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379` |
| `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` | `clickhouse`, and passed to the gateway |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `obleth`, `control-plane`, `obleth-provisioner` |
| `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` | `control-plane` (break-glass admin, at least 8 characters) |
| `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` | `control-plane`, also passed as `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (at least 32 characters) |
| `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `grafana` (`observability` profile only) |

`.env.example` ships development values for all of them, including
`REDIS_PASSWORD=dev-redis-password`. Replace every one before any shared
deployment:

```bash
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
REDIS_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)      # must be URL-safe; hex is simplest
CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=...                      # at least 8 characters
DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
```

(Write the generated values into `.env`; Compose does not run shell commands in
`.env`.)

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Shutdown
chunks.text:
The `obleth` service sets `stop_grace_period: 345s`: the 300 s
`OBLETH_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS` drain, 20 s for the telemetry flush, 10 s for the
OTLP exporter, and a margin. If you raise `OBLETH_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS`, raise
`stop_grace_period` by the same amount in your override file. See
[Shutdown & Timeouts](/docs/operations/graceful-shutdown-and-timeouts).

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Standalone datastores
chunks.text:
`datastores.compose.yml` runs Postgres, Redis, and ClickHouse on their own as a
durable tier for a gateway that runs elsewhere (a Helm install with bundled
datastores disabled, or a bare binary):

```bash
cd deploy/docker
cp datastores.env.example datastores.env   # change every password
docker compose --env-file datastores.env -f datastores.compose.yml up -d
```

The project is named `obleth-datastores`. Ports publish on `BIND_ADDR`
(default `127.0.0.1`); set it to a private interface address to allow an
off-host gateway, and protect it with a firewall. Redis runs with AOF
(`--appendfsync everysec`) and `--requirepass`. Point the gateway at it with:

```bash
OBLETH_DATABASE_URL=postgres://obleth:POSTGRES_PASSWORD@DB_HOST:5432/obleth
OBLETH_REDIS_URL=redis://:REDIS_PASSWORD@DB_HOST:6379
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_URL=http://DB_HOST:8123
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_USER=obleth
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_DB=obleth
```

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Starting the stack
chunks.text:
```bash
cd obleth-gateway/deploy/docker
cp .env.example .env          # then change every password and secret
docker compose up -d --build
```

`.env.example` sets `COMPOSE_PROFILES=benchmark,edge,observability`, so that one
command also starts the benchmark backend, HAProxy, and the observability stack.
Leave `COMPOSE_PROFILES` empty for the core services only, or opt in ad hoc:

```bash
docker compose --profile slurm up -d
```

The first-party services declare both an `image:` (published to
`ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/`) and a `build:` context. `docker compose
pull && docker compose up -d` runs the published images; `docker compose up
--build` builds from the working tree. Pin a release in `.env`:

```bash
OBLETH_VERSION=v1.3.0
OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION=v1.3.0   # only if you run the compressor profile
```

`OBLETH_VERSION` defaults to `latest` (newest stable release); `dev` tracks edge
builds. The compression sidecar has its own tag variable because edge builds
skip it.

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Stopping
chunks.text:
```bash
docker compose down
```

`docker compose down -v` also deletes the `pgdata`, `redisdata`, and `chdata`
volumes: every tenant, key, model, and all usage history. Take a
[backup](/docs/operations/backup-restore) first.

chunks.title: Docker Compose Reference
chunks.heading: Variables Compose does not forward
chunks.text:
The `obleth` service hardcodes these values, so setting them in `.env` has no
effect:

| Variable | Fixed value |
| --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `1024` |
| `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `32` |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_HISTORY_SECS` | `3600` |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_ALGORITHM` | `hierarchical` |
| `OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN` | `true` (the `OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN` line in `.env.example` is not read) |
| `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN`, `OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN`, `OBLETH_METRICS_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:8080`, `0.0.0.0:9180`, `0.0.0.0:9091` |
| `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_URL` | `http://clickhouse:8123` |
| `RUST_LOG` | `info,obleth=debug` |

`OBLETH_UPSTREAM_POOL_IDLE_SECS`, `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TCP_KEEPALIVE_SECS`, the
provisioner's other `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_*` variables, and `OBLETH_PORT_SPAN`
are not passed at all, so their binary defaults apply.

`PUT /api/v1/capacity` adjusts the global ceiling at runtime, but only on the
replica that serves the call and only until the next restart. To change any of
these values durably, add your own Compose file that overrides the service's
`environment:` and include it after the main file:

```yaml
# deploy/docker/compose.tuning.yml
services:
  obleth:
    environment:
      OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT: "64"
      OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN: "false"
```

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f compose.tuning.yml up -d obleth
```

To avoid repeating `-f` on every command, set
`COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:compose.tuning.yml` in `.env` (use `;` as the
separator

Container ports that are only `expose`d to the Comp

chunks.title: Endpoints & Ports
chunks.heading: HAProxy frontend
chunks.text:
When running the Docker Compose `edge` profile. The Helm chart does not deploy HAProxy; on Kubernetes the same role is filled by the obleth Service plus the chart's optional Ingress.

| Port | Protocol | Backend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `80` | HTTP | obleth data plane (`8080`) |
| `8404` | HTTP | HAProxy's own `/metrics` and `/stats` (in-network only) |

The shipped `deploy/docker/haproxy.cfg` binds plaintext `:80` only and
round-robins across the obleth backend servers. It is a reference topology that
assumes TLS is terminated in front of it; to make HAProxy the TLS edge itself,
add a `bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/ssl/private/obleth.pem` frontend and mount the
certificate. See [HAProxy](/docs/reference/haproxy).

chunks.title: Endpoints & Ports
chunks.heading: Health check
chunks.text:
```bash
# Management API health
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/health

# Data plane liveness (no auth required)
curl http://localhost/health          # via HAProxy (edge profile)
# curl http://localhost:8088/health   # direct host port in Docker Compose
# curl http://localhost:8080/health   # native cargo run (binds :8080 on the host)

# Metrics
curl http://localhost:9091/metrics | head -20
```

The data plane's `/v1/models` route requires a tenant API key. Use `/health` for a
liveness probe instead.

chunks.text:
All Services are `ClusterIP`; `<release>` is the Helm release name. The
optional Ingress routes to the data-plane port only.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `<release>-obleth` data plane (`proxy`) | `8080` | Ingress target |
| `<release>-obleth` Management API (`admin`) | `9180` | Internal only. With `networkPolicy.enabled`, reachable only from the control plane and provisioner |
| `<release>-obleth` metrics (`metrics`) | `9091` | Prometheus scrape and ServiceMonitor target |
| `<release>-control-plane` | `3000` | Dashboard (`controlPlane.enabled`) |
| `<release>-compressor` | `8080` | Compression sidecar (`compressor.enabled`) |
| `<release>-postgres` | `5432` | Bundled Postgres (`postgres.enabled`) |
| `<release>-redis` | `6379` | Bundled Redis (`redis.enabled`) |
| `<release>-clickhouse` | `8123`, `9000` | Bundled ClickHouse (`clickhouse.enabled`) |
| `<release>-benchmark-backend` | `8081` | Test upstream (`benchmarkBackend.enabled`) |

The provisioner has no Service; it only makes outbound calls.

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Admission and fairshare
chunks.text:
| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `1024` | Total in-flight ceiling across all model pools, per gateway process. It is a safety ceiling, not a fairness input; keep it above the sum of the pool sizes you expect. `PUT /api/v1/capacity` changes it at runtime on the replica that serves the call only, and the change is lost on restart. | fixed (`1024`) |
| `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `32` | Pool size for a model that has no `max_in_flight` of its own. Each model has its own pool. | fixed (`32`) |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_ALGORITHM` | `hierarchical` | `hierarchical` (group, then tenant, then key) or `weighted`. | fixed (`hierarchical`) |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_HISTORY_SECS` | `3600` | Seconds of scheduler history kept in memory for the Fairshare activity chart, sampled every 2 s and served by `GET /api/v1/fairshare/history`. `0` disables the sampler. | fixed (`3600`) |
| `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `60` | Longest a request waits in the fairshare queue. On timeout the gateway returns `503` "timed out waiting for model capacity" with `Retry-After: 5`. `0` or an invalid value uses the default. | `.env` (`60`) |

Pools, weights, and ceilings are explained in
[Fairshare Engine](/docs/concepts/fairshare-engine).

chunks.text:
| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |

| `OBLETH_SLACK_ALERT_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS` | `300` | Seeds the per-alert cooldown until alert settings are saved. | `.env` (`300`) |
| `OBLETH_OTEL_ENDPOINT` | unset (tracing off) | OTLP/HTTP collector base URL; spans are posted to `{url}/v1/traces`. With the Compose `observability` profile, use `http://jaeger:4318`. | `.env` (empty) |
| `RUST_LOG` | `info,obleth=debug` | Log filter (`tracing` `EnvFilter` syntax). The built-in default applies only when unset or unparseable. | fixed (`info,obleth=debug`); Helm sets `info,obleth=info` |

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Auto-routing classifier
chunks.text:
These three seed the `auto` router settings on first boot only. Once routing
settings are saved (Settings → Routing, or `PUT /api/v1/settings/auto-router`),
the stored values are authoritative. See
[Auto Model Routing](/docs/guides/auto-model-routing).

| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_ENABLED` | `false` | Enables the intent classifier for `model: "auto"`. | `.env` (`false`) |
| `OBLETH_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_MODEL` | unset | Registered model used to classify requests into routing tags. | `.env` (empty) |
| `OBLETH_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_TIMEOUT_MS` | `250` | Per-request classifier timeout. On timeout the request is routed without tags. | `.env` (`250`) |

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: benchmark-backend
chunks.text:
The GPU-free OpenAI-compatible fixture used by the `benchmark` Compose profile,
the Helm `benchmarkBackend` Deployment, and [obench](/docs/guides/benchmark-harness).

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:8081` | Bind address. |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_TTFT_MS` | `20` | Simulated time to first token. |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_TOKEN_MS` | `5` | Simulated inter-token delay. Compose and Helm set `3`. |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_DEFAULT_OUTPUT` | `64` | Output tokens when the request sets no `max_tokens`. |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_CONCURRENCY` | `10000` | Concurrent requests served before callers queue. Compose and Helm set `256` to simulate a saturated backend. |

Each variable also accepts a `MOCK_` spelling (`MOCK_LISTEN`, `MOCK_TTFT_MS`,
and so on) as a fallback.

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Compose-only variables
chunks.text:
These are read by `docker compose` for substitution into
`deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml`, not by any obleth binary. See
[Docker Compose](/docs/reference/docker-compose).

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPOSE_PROFILES` | `benchmark,edge,observability` in `.env.example` | Optional services to start. |
| `OBLETH_VERSION` | `latest` | Image tag for obleth, obleth-provisioner, control-plane, and benchmark-backend. Pin a release such as `v1.3.0`; `dev` tracks edge builds. |
| `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` | `latest` | Image tag for the compression sidecar, set separately because edge builds skip it. Set it to the same `vX.Y.Z` as `OBLETH_VERSION` for a release deploy. |

| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | required (`dev-redis-password` in `.env.example`) | Password the bundled Redis requires, composed into `OBLETH_REDIS_URL`. Use URL-safe characters, for example `openssl rand -hex 32`. |
| `CLICKHOUSE_USER` / `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` / `CLICKHOUSE_DB` | `obleth` / required / `obleth` | Bundled ClickHouse credentials, also passed to the gateway. |
| `COMPRESSOR_CPUS` | `4` | CPU quota and onnxruntime thread count for the sidecar. |
| `COMPRESSOR_SOURCE` / `COMPRESSOR_MODEL_ID` / `COMPRESSOR_ONNX_FILE` | `onnx` / `chopratejas/kompress-v2-base` / `onnx/kompress-fp32.onnx` | Build arguments sele

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Compression sidecar
chunks.text:
The neural prose-compression sidecar is configured only through the
environment. `GET /api/v1/settings/compressor` reports its live status.

| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL` | unset (neural stage off) | Sidecar base URL, for example `http://compressor:8080`. Unset or empty disables the neural stage of the [compression boon](/docs/guides/model-boons); the lossless structural passes still run. | `.env` (empty) |
| `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_TIMEOUT_MS` | `800` | Per-request scoring timeout. On timeout or error the text is left uncompressed. The Management API status probe uses this value with a floor of 2000 ms. | `.env` (empty, so `800`) |

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Control plane
chunks.text:
| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | required | Management API token. Requests fail if it is unset. |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:9180` | Management API base URL. Compose sets `http://obleth:9180`. |
| `OBLETH_PROXY_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Data-plane base URL used by the portal pages, the Playground, the assistant, and MCP probes. Compose sets `http://obleth:8080`. |
| `DATABASE_URL` | required | Postgres URL for the dashboard's auth tables (`user`, `session`, `account`, `verification`). Normally the same database as the gateway. |
| `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` | none (Compose and Helm default `admin@example.com`) | Email of the break-glass admin seeded on boot when no active admin exists. Must be an email address. |
| `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` | none | Break-glass admin password, at least 8 characters, stored hashed. When it or the email is unset, no admin is seeded (for example, an SSO-only deployment). |
| `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` | required | Session signing secret, at least 32 characters. Used when `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is unset. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` | Auth-library secret, at least 32 characters. Compose and Helm set it to `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET`. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` | Browser-facing dashboard URL. Logins are accepted only from this origin (plus `TRUSTED_ORIGINS`), and OIDC redirect URIs are built from it.

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: obleth-provisioner
chunks.text:
The provisioner reads only its Management API connection and cadence from the
environment. The slurmrestd URL, API version, user, JWT, and the master enable
switch are set in Settings → Slurm and fetched from the Management API on every
tick. See [Slurm Provisioning](/docs/guides/slurm-provisioning).

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | required | Management API token (the same value as the gateway's). |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:9180` | Management API base URL. Compose sets `http://obleth:9180`; Helm sets the release's obleth Service. |
| `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_INTERVAL_SECS` | `15` | Reconcile tick interval. |
| `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `5` | Per-replica health-probe timeout. |
| `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `600` | Timeout for the one-token warmup request sent to each replica after promotion, so the first real request does not pay the cold-start cost. `0` disables warmup. |
| `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_LOST_RETENTION_SECS` | `900` | How long `lost` replica rows are kept before garbage collection. |
| `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_RESTART_AFTER_FAILURES` | `20` | Self-heal threshold: restart a `healthy` replica after this many net failing probe ticks while its Slurm job still reports RUNNING. The counter decays on each passing probe, so 20 ticks at the default interval is about five minutes of sustained failure. At most one restart per model per tick. `0` disables self-heal. |

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth has no configuration file. Each process reads its settings from the
environment at startup; settings that change at runtime (routing, boons,
alerts, energy, Slurm connection, retention) live in Postgres and are managed
from the dashboard or the [Management API](/docs/reference/management-api).

This page lists the 69 runtime variables read by the four first-party binaries:

| Binary | Image | Variables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `obleth` (data plane, Management API, metrics) | `obleth` | 46 |
| `obleth-provisioner` (Slurm reconciler) | `obleth-provisioner` | 8, plus the shared `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` |
| control plane (Next.js dashboard) | `control-plane` | 10, plus the shared `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` and `OBLETH_ADMIN_BASE_URL` |
| `benchmark-backend` (GPU-free test upstream) | `benchmark-backend` | 5 |

The **Compose** column records how `deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml` sets each
gateway variable:

- **`.env`**: forwarded from `deploy/docker/.env`, with the default shown.
- **fixed**: hardcoded in the Compose file. Setting it in `.env` has no effect.
- **composed**: built from other `.env` values (for example, the Redis URL from `REDIS_PASSWORD`).
- **not set**: Compose does not pass it, so the binary default applies.

See [Docker Compose](/docs/reference/docker-compose#variables-compose-does-not-forward)
for how to change a fixed or unset value, and
[Helm Values](/docs/reference/helm-values#gateway-environment-mapping) for the
chart value behind each variable.

Boolean vari

chunks.title: Environment Variables
chunks.heading: Reliability and shutdown
chunks.text:
| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN` | `true` | When Redis is unavailable, admit requests without budget checks (`true`) or reject them (`false`). Strict boolean: any value other than the accepted spellings aborts startup. | fixed (`true`) |
| `OBLETH_WAL_PATH` | `./obleth-telemetry.wal` | Telemetry write-ahead log. Usage batches spill here while ClickHouse is unreachable and replay on recovery. Must be writable by the runtime user (uid `10001` in the image). Helm sets `/var/lib/obleth/telemetry.wal`. | `.env` (`/tmp/obleth-telemetry.wal`) |
| `OBLETH_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS` | `300` | On SIGTERM the gateway stops accepting connections and waits up to this long for in-flight requests, streams included, before flushing telemetry and exiting. Keep the orchestrator's stop timeout above it. See [Shutdown & Timeouts](/docs/operations/graceful-shutdown-and-timeouts). | `.env` (`300`) |

chunks.heading: Security
chunks.text:
| Variable | Default | Purpose | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | required | Bearer token for the Management API, shared with the provisioner and the control plane. The gateway refuses to start when it is unset or blank. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. | `.env` (required) |
| `OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | unset | Base64 of 32 random bytes (`openssl rand -base64 32`). Encrypts model `api_key`, MCP `auth_header`, and the Slurm JWT at rest with AES-256-GCM. | `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` | unset (JWT path off) | JSON array of trusted identity-provider issuers whose JWT access tokens the data plane accepts alongside API keys. Read at boot only. A value that fails to parse stops the process with exit code 2. See [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens). | `.env` (empty) |
| `OBLETH_BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | `false` | Outbound URL policy for operator-supplied destinations (model `api_base`, MCP `upstream_url`, JWKS URLs). By default private, LAN, loopback, and CGNAT targets are allowed and only link-local and cloud-metadata ranges (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`) are bl
