chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Admin API protection
chunks.text: The admin API (`:9180`) should not be exposed via HAProxy. Keep it on the internal network only and use Kubernetes NetworkPolicy or firewall rules to restrict access.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Docker Compose (edge profile)
chunks.text:
```bash
cd deploy/docker
docker compose --profile edge up -d
```

The shipped image is `haproxy:3.2`. It starts on port `80` with the obleth data
plane as the backend; TLS is not enabled by default.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Health check
chunks.text:
HAProxy can health-check obleth pods using the `/health` endpoint:

```nginx
backend obleth_pods
    option httpchk GET /health
    http-check expect string "ok"
    server obleth1 obleth:8080 check inter 5s fall 3 rise 2
```

The data plane's `/health` route needs no authentication and returns the literal
body `ok`.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: HAProxy is the reference TLS terminator and load balancer for obleth. It ships in the Docker Compose stack under the `edge` profile. The Helm chart does not deploy HAProxy — on Kubernetes the same role is filled by a Service plus the chart's optional [Ingress](/docs/reference/helm-values#ingress).

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Shipped configuration
chunks.text:
The data-plane section of `deploy/docker/haproxy.cfg`, with its comments
shortened:

```nginx
global
    log stdout format raw local0
    maxconn 50000

# Re-resolve backend hostnames at runtime via Docker's embedded DNS, so
# recreating the obleth container (new IP) does not leave HAProxy health-checking
# a dead address. Kubernetes Services track pod IPs natively, so this is a
# Compose-only concern.
resolvers docker
    nameserver dns 127.0.0.11:53
    resolve_retries 3
    timeout resolve 1s
    timeout retry  1s
    hold valid 10s

defaults
    mode http
    log global
    option httplog
    timeout connect 5s
    timeout client  300s
    timeout server  300s
    # streaming responses: don't buffer
    option http-no-delay

frontend obleth_front
    # Plaintext :80 — a managed edge LB is assumed to terminate TLS in front.
    bind *:80
    default_backend obleth_pods

backend obleth_pods
    balance roundrobin
    # one pod in compose; in prod this is the obleth fleet
    server obleth1 obleth:8080 check resolvers docker init-addr last,libc,none
```

To balance across several gateways, add one `server` line per instance to
`obleth_pods`. The stats frontend that follows in the same file is shown under
[Stats page](#stats-page).

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Stats page
chunks.text:
The Compose `edge` profile also exposes HAProxy's built-in Prometheus exporter
and human stats UI on `:8404` (`/metrics` and `/stats`). The `/stats` page is
protected with HTTP basic auth so it can't be browsed anonymously if the port is
ever published:

```nginx
frontend stats
    bind *:8404
    mode http
    http-request use-service prometheus-exporter if { path /metrics }
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s
    stats realm obleth\ stats
    stats auth ${HAPROXY_STATS_USER}:${HAPROXY_STATS_PASSWORD}
```

Set the credentials in `deploy/docker/.env`:

```bash
HAPROXY_STATS_USER=admin
HAPROXY_STATS_PASSWORD=...   # change from the dev example
```

The `/metrics` endpoint is left unauthenticated so Prometheus can scrape it; keep
`:8404` on the internal network and do not publish it publicly.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Streaming requirements
chunks.text:
obleth uses HTTP/1.1 streaming for `text/event-stream` (SSE) responses. HAProxy must not buffer streaming responses. Key settings:

- `timeout client 300s` and `timeout server 300s` (must be >= `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS`)
- `option http-no-delay` — forwards each chunk as it arrives instead of coalescing it
- Do not enable `compression` — it buffers the response

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: TLS termination
chunks.text:
The shipped frontend is plaintext `:80` only, on the assumption that a managed
edge load balancer terminates TLS in front of it. To make HAProxy the TLS edge
instead, mount your certificate (PEM format, certificate + private key in a
single file) and enable TLS on the frontend:

```nginx
frontend obleth_front
    bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/ssl/private/obleth.pem
    bind *:80
    http-request redirect scheme https unless { ssl_fc }
    default_backend obleth_pods
```

For Docker Compose, mount the cert and publish `443`:

```yaml
haproxy:
  ports: ["80:80", "443:443"]
  volumes:
    - ./certs/obleth.pem:/etc/ssl/private/obleth.pem:ro
```

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Autoscaling (HPA)
chunks.text:
```yaml
hpa:
  enabled: false
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 20
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
```

When enabled, the chart omits `replicas` and renders an `autoscaling/v2`
HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU. Because each replica enforces its own pools and
ceiling, scaling from 2 to 8 pods raises the aggregate concurrency reaching the
upstream fourfold. Size `globalMaxInFlight` and the model pools so that
`maxReplicas` times those numbers stays within what the upstream can absorb.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Benchmark backend
chunks.text:
```yaml
benchmarkBackend:
  enabled: true           # disable in production
  ttftMs: 20
  tokenMs: 3
  concurrency: 256
```

With `enabled: false` you must set `obleth.upstreamBaseUrl`.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: ClickHouse
chunks.text:
```yaml
clickhouse:
  enabled: true
  image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8
  db: obleth
  user: obleth
  password: ""            # REQUIRED when enabled
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "500m", memory: "2Gi" }
    limits: { cpu: "1", memory: "4Gi" }
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 20Gi
    storageClass: ""
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
  external:
    url: ""               # http://host:8123
```

Readiness: `GET /ping` on 8123.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Compression sidecar
chunks.text:
```yaml
compressor:
  enabled: false
  replicas: 1
  numThreads: 4               # keep equal to resources.limits.cpu
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/obleth-compressor
    tag: ""                   # empty -> v{appVersion}
    pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "4", memory: 1536Mi }
    limits: { cpu: "4", memory: 2Gi }
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 5
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
```

When enabled, the chart sets `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL` on the gateway. The data
plane fails open if the sidecar is unreachable. Probes: readiness `GET /health`
(delay 30 s, every 10 s), liveness `GET /health` (delay 60 s, every 30 s).

A single inference saturates near four cores and each pod holds the model
(about 900 MB) in memory, so scale by adding replicas of 4 to 8 cores rather
than growing one pod. Keep `numThreads`, `requests.cpu`, and `limits.cpu`
equal; CPU autoscaling depends on the limit being set.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Control plane
chunks.text:
```yaml
controlPlane:
  enabled: true
  replicas: 1
  dashboardPassword: ""             # REQUIRED unless existingSecret; at least 8 characters
  dashboardSessionSecret: ""        # REQUIRED unless existingSecret; at least 32 characters
  existingSecret: ""
  databaseUrl: ""                   # empty -> the bundled Postgres
  betterAuthUrl: ""                 # browser-facing URL, e.g. https://dashboard.example.com
  trustedOrigins: ""                # comma-separated extra login origins
  dashboardAdminEmail: admin@example.com
  oidcProviders: ""                 # JSON array; empty = break-glass admin only
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "100m", memory: "256Mi" }
    limits: { cpu: "1", memory: "512Mi" }
```

The dashboard credentials and auth settings go into a dedicated Secret
(`<release>-control-plane-secret`) injected with `envFrom`.
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is set to `dashboardSessionSecret`. The Deployment sets
`OBLETH_ADMIN_BASE_URL` and `OBLETH_PROXY_BASE_URL` to the obleth Service and
reads `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` from the obleth Secret. Probes: readiness
`GET /login` (delay 5 s, every 10 s) and liveness `GET /login` (delay 15 s,
every 20 s).

An `oidcProviders` entry takes `providerId`, `displayName`, `discoveryUrl`,
`clientId`, `clientSecret`, and `scopes`, plus optional `claims` (map `email`,
`name`, or `image` to another claim), `overrideUserInfo` (re-apply the profile
on each sign-in), and `authentication: "basic"` for IdPs that accept only HTTP
Basic at the token e

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Datastores
chunks.text:
Each bundled datastore supports three storage modes:

| Mode | Setting | Data on restart |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent (default) | `persistence.enabled: true` | kept on a PVC |
| Ephemeral | `persistence.enabled: false` | lost (`emptyDir`) |
| External | `enabled: false` plus `external.url` | managed by you |

Bundled datastore Deployments use the `Recreate` strategy so a new pod never
attaches a `ReadWriteOnce` PVC the old pod still holds. Each has a readiness
probe every 5 s with a 3 s timeout. Ready-made overlays are in
`deploy/k8s/obleth/examples/` (`values-persistent.yaml`,
`values-ephemeral.yaml`, `values-external.yaml`, `values-production.yaml`).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Gateway
chunks.text:
```yaml
obleth:
  replicas: 1
  globalMaxInFlight: 1024          # total ceiling across all model pools, per replica
  defaultModelMaxInFlight: 32      # pool size for a model with no max_in_flight
  fairshareHistorySecs: 3600       # activity-chart history (2 s samples); 0 disables
  failOpen: true
  adminToken: ""                   # REQUIRED unless existingSecret
  encryptionKey: ""                # base64 of 32 bytes; empty stores upstream secrets in plaintext
  apiKeyPepper: ""                 # optional; changing it invalidates issued keys
  jwtIssuers: ""                   # optional JSON array; empty disables the JWT path
  existingSecret: ""               # name of a pre-created Secret
  allowedPrivateCidrs: ""          # only used in strict outbound-URL mode
  upstreamBaseUrl: ""              # empty -> in-chart benchmark backend
  otelEndpoint: ""                 # OTLP/HTTP base URL; empty disables tracing
  slackWebhookUrl: ""              # first-boot seed for alerts
  slackAlertMinIntervalSecs: 300
  modelHealthEnabled: true
  modelHealthIntervalSecs: 900
  modelHealthTimeoutSecs: 30
  modelHealthRetentionDays: 30
  usageRetentionDays: 180
  shutdownGraceSecs: 300           # keep below terminationGracePeriodSeconds (345)
  redisRewarmSecs: 300             # Postgres -> Redis re-push interval; 0 disables the timer
  upstreamTimeoutSecs: 300         # upstream wait for response headers (TTFB when streaming)
  upstreamReadTimeoutSecs: ""      # empty -> upstream

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Identity tokens (`jwtIssuers`)
chunks.text:
A JSON array, as one string, of trusted issuers. Empty disables the JWT path.

```yaml
obleth:
  jwtIssuers: '[{"issuer":"https://idp.example.com","audience":"obleth","tenant":"cli-users"}]'
```

The gateway reads it at boot only. With `existingSecret`, put it under
`OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` and restart the Deployment after changing it. Field
reference: [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Images
chunks.text:
```yaml
image:
  obleth: ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/obleth
  benchmarkBackend: ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/benchmark-backend
  controlPlane: ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/control-plane
  provisioner: ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/obleth-provisioner
  tag: ""                     # empty -> v{appVersion}, i.e. v1.3.0
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

Leaving `tag` empty keeps the images in lockstep with the chart. Override it
only to test another tag (`dev` for edge builds). The compression sidecar has
its own `compressor.image` block.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Ingress
chunks.text:
```yaml
ingress:
  enabled: false
  className: ""
  host: obleth.example.com
  servicePort: 8080
  annotations: {}
  tls: []          # e.g. [{ secretName: obleth-tls, hosts: [obleth.example.com] }]
```

The Ingress routes to the obleth Service on `servicePort`. Keep it on `8080`;
never expose `9180`. The chart does not deploy HAProxy.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Minimal production values
chunks.text:
This inlines secrets for brevity. For a hardened install, use pre-created
Secrets and start from
[`values-production.yaml`](https://github.com/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/blob/main/deploy/k8s/obleth/examples/values-production.yaml).

```yaml
obleth:
  adminToken: "REPLACE_WITH_openssl_rand_hex_32"
  encryptionKey: "REPLACE_WITH_openssl_rand_base64_32"
  upstreamBaseUrl: "http://inference.inference.svc.cluster.local:8000/v1"
  replicas: 2
  # Each replica enforces its own pools and ceiling: two replicas admit up to
  # 2 x 1024 in total, and 2 x each model's pool size per model.
  globalMaxInFlight: 1024

postgres:
  enabled: false
  external:
    url: "postgres://obleth:PASSWORD@pg.example.internal:5432/obleth"

redis:
  enabled: false
  external:
    url: "redis://:PASSWORD@redis.example.internal:6379"

clickhouse:
  enabled: false
  external:
    url: "http://clickhouse.example.internal:8123"

benchmarkBackend:
  enabled: false

controlPlane:
  dashboardAdminEmail: "admin@example.com"
  dashboardPassword: "REPLACE_ME"
  dashboardSessionSecret: "REPLACE_WITH_openssl_rand_hex_32"
  betterAuthUrl: "https://dashboard.example.com"

serviceMonitor:
  enabled: true

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx
  host: obleth.example.com
  tls:
    - secretName: obleth-tls
      hosts:
        - obleth.example.com
```

With external ClickHouse, supply its password as `clickhouse.password` (it is
rendered into `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`) or through `existingSecret`.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Monitoring
chunks.text:
```yaml
serviceMonitor:
  enabled: false   # requires the Prometheus Operator CRDs
```

The ServiceMonitor scrapes the `metrics` port every 5 s. Metric names are in
[Prometheus Metrics](/docs/reference/prometheus-metrics).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: NetworkPolicy
chunks.text:
```yaml
networkPolicy:
  enabled: false
```

Requires a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy. When enabled, the chart renders
ingress rules:

| Target | Allowed from |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled Postgres `5432` | obleth pods, and control-plane pods when `controlPlane.enabled` |
| Bundled Redis `6379` | obleth pods |
| Bundled ClickHouse `8123`, `9000` | obleth pods |
| obleth `8080` (data plane) | any source |
| obleth `9091` (metrics) | any source, so a Prometheus in another namespace can scrape it |
| obleth `9180` (Management API) | control-plane and provisioner pods (rendered when either is enabled) |

Datastore policies are rendered only for bundled datastores.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Outbound URL policy
chunks.text:
The default policy allows private and LAN destinations, so `api_base` values
pointing at in-cluster Services work without `allowedPrivateCidrs`. The chart
does not set `OBLETH_BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORKS`; to enable strict mode, add
`OBLETH_BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORKS=1` to the `existingSecret` and list trusted
ranges in `allowedPrivateCidrs`. See [Security](/docs/operations/security).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The chart lives in `deploy/k8s/obleth/` and is published as an OCI chart at
`oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth`. The chart version and `appVersion`
are both `1.3.0`.

```bash
helm install obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth \
  --version 1.3.0 \
  --namespace obleth --create-namespace \
  --set obleth.adminToken=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  --set postgres.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set redis.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set clickhouse.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set controlPlane.dashboardPassword='change-me-now' \
  --set controlPlane.dashboardSessionSecret=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  -f my-values.yaml
```

`--set` values end up in shell history and in the release record. For
production, create the Secrets yourself and reference them with
[`existingSecret`](#pre-created-secrets-existingsecret).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Postgres
chunks.text:
```yaml
postgres:
  enabled: true
  image: postgres:16
  user: obleth
  password: ""            # REQUIRED when enabled
  db: obleth
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "250m", memory: "512Mi" }
    limits: { cpu: "500m", memory: "1Gi" }
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 10Gi
    storageClass: ""      # "" = cluster default
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
  external:
    url: ""               # postgres://user:pass@host:5432/obleth
```

Readiness: `pg_isready`. Postgres is the configuration source of truth; keep
persistence on for anything you care about.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Pre-created Secrets (`existingSecret`)
chunks.text:
When `obleth.existingSecret` names a Secret, the chart renders no Secret of its
own and reads that one instead. It must provide:

```
OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN
OBLETH_DATABASE_URL
OBLETH_REDIS_URL              # redis://:PASSWORD@host:6379
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY
OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER
OBLETH_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS            # optional
POSTGRES_PASSWORD             # when postgres.enabled
REDIS_PASSWORD                # when redis.enabled; must match the password in OBLETH_REDIS_URL
```

With bundled ClickHouse, `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` is also the password the
ClickHouse container uses.

`controlPlane.existingSecret` works the same way and must provide
`DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`, `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `TRUSTED_ORIGINS`,
`DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL`, and `OIDC_PROVIDERS`. `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` falls back
to `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` when omitted. See
[`values-production.yaml`](https://github.com/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/blob/main/deploy/k8s/obleth/examples/values-production.yaml)
and the [Self-Hosting](/docs/guides/self-hosting) production scenario.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Reaching Slurm compute nodes
chunks.text:
Applied to the obleth and provisioner pods only. All empty by default, which
leaves cluster DNS unchanged.

```yaml
nodeResolution:
  hostAliases: []
  #  - ip: "10.0.0.25"
  #    hostnames: ["gpu-node-01", "gpu-node-01.cluster.example.edu"]
  dnsConfig: {}
  #  nameservers: ["10.0.0.10"]
  #  searches: ["cluster.example.edu"]
  #  options: [{ name: ndots, value: "2" }]
  dnsPolicy: ""           # e.g. "None" when dnsConfig fully specifies nameservers
```

Node address overrides can also be set at runtime in Settings → Slurm. See
[Slurm Provisioning](/docs/guides/slurm-provisioning).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Redis
chunks.text:
```yaml
redis:
  enabled: true
  image: redis:7
  password: ""            # REQUIRED when enabled; hex recommended
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi" }
    limits: { cpu: "200m", memory: "512Mi" }
  maxmemory: 400mb
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 1Gi
    storageClass: ""
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
  external:
    url: ""               # redis://:PASSWORD@host:6379
```

The bundled Redis runs with AOF, `--requirepass`, `--maxmemory` from
`redis.maxmemory`, and `--maxmemory-policy volatile-lru`: only keys with a TTL
can be evicted. API keys, model routes, and MCP servers have no TTL and are
never evicted. The response cache, compression originals, cached query
embeddings, per-minute buckets, and the term-budget counters
(`obleth:term_usage:*`, 1-year TTL) all carry TTLs and can be evicted under
memory pressure; an evicted term counter restarts that budget period's usage
at zero. See [Redis Layout](/docs/reference/redis-layout#key-prefixes). Keep
`maxmemory` at about 80% of the memory limit and size it so eviction does not
occur in normal operation. Readiness: `redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" --no-auth-warning ping`.

An external Redis must be a single primary that requires a password; Redis
Cluster is not supported. Redis is rebuilt from Postgres after data loss. See
[Redis Layout](/docs/reference/redis-layout).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Rendered pod settings
chunks.text:
The obleth Deployment is not configurable beyond the values above; these are
fixed in `templates/obleth.yaml`:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` | `345` (300 s drain + 20 s telemetry + 10 s OTLP + margin) |
| `lifecycle.preStop` | `sleep 5`, so endpoint removal reaches Services and ingresses before the process stops accepting |
| `startupProbe` | `GET /health` on `proxy`, every 5 s, 30 failures (about 150 s for migrations and the Redis warm-up) |
| `readinessProbe` | `GET /health`, initial delay 5 s, every 5 s |
| `livenessProbe` | `GET /health`, initial delay 10 s, every 10 s |
| WAL volume | `emptyDir` named `wal` at `/var/lib/obleth`. Spilled telemetry survives container restarts, not pod deletion |
| `checksum/secret` annotation | SHA-256 of the rendered Secret, so a changed chart Secret rolls the pods. With `existingSecret` it is constant; restart the Deployment yourself after editing that Secret |
| Service ports | `proxy` 8080, `admin` 9180, `metrics` 9091 |

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Required values
chunks.text:
Rendering fails with a clear message when any of these is missing:

| Value | Required when |
| --- | --- |
| `obleth.adminToken` | always, unless `obleth.existingSecret` is set |
| `postgres.password` | `postgres.enabled: true` |
| `redis.password` | `redis.enabled: true` |
| `clickhouse.password` | `clickhouse.enabled: true` |
| `controlPlane.dashboardPassword` | `controlPlane.enabled: true`, unless `controlPlane.existingSecret` is set |
| `controlPlane.dashboardSessionSecret` | same as above; at least 32 characters |
| `postgres.external.url` | `postgres.enabled: false` |
| `redis.external.url` | `redis.enabled: false` |
| `clickhouse.external.url` | `clickhouse.enabled: false` |
| `obleth.upstreamBaseUrl` | `benchmarkBackend.enabled: false` |

`redis.password` is embedded unescaped in `OBLETH_REDIS_URL`, so rendering
also fails if it contains `@`, `:`, `/`, `?`, `#`, `%`, or whitespace. Use a hex
value (`openssl rand -hex 16`).

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Security contexts (Pod Security Standard)
chunks.text:
```yaml
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    drop: [ALL]
  runAsNonRoot: true
  # readOnlyRootFilesystem: true   # opt-in
```

Applied to the obleth, control-plane, provisioner, compressor, and
benchmark-backend pods. The defaults satisfy the Kubernetes
[restricted](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/#restricted)
Pod Security Standard. No UID is pinned: the images run as non-root users
(obleth `10001`, control-plane `1000`). The bundled datastores are excluded
because their official images manage their own users.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Slurm provisioner
chunks.text:
```yaml
provisioner:
  enabled: false
  intervalSecs: 15
  restartAfterFailures: 20
  logLevel: "info,obleth_provisioner=debug"
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "50m", memory: "64Mi" }
    limits: { cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi" }
```

This only controls whether the reconciler is deployed; the slurmrestd
connection and the master enable switch are set in Settings → Slurm. The
Deployment is a singleton (`replicas: 1`, `Recreate`, not configurable) with
`terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60` so a tick can finish, no probes, and no
Service. It sets `OBLETH_ADMIN_BASE_URL` to the obleth Service,
`OBLETH_PROVISIONER_INTERVAL_SECS`, `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_RESTART_AFTER_FAILURES`,
and `RUST_LOG` from these values, and reads `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` from the obleth
Secret.

`restartAfterFailures` restarts a `healthy` replica whose Slurm job still
reports RUNNING after that many net failing probe ticks; the counter decays on
each passing probe, so 20 ticks at 15 s is about five minutes of sustained
failure. At most one restart per model per tick; `0` disables self-heal.

chunks.title: Helm Values
chunks.heading: Spread and disruption protection
chunks.text:
```yaml
affinity:
  antiAffinity: soft      # soft | hard | ""
podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: true
  minAvailable: 1
```

`soft` prefers distinct nodes but still schedules on a single-node cluster;
`hard` requires distinct nodes; `""` disables anti-affinity.

The PodDisruptionBudget is rendered only when `enabled` is true and the
effective minimum replica count is greater than 1: `hpa.minReplicas` when the
HPA is enabled, otherwise `obleth.replicas`. A budget of `minAvailable: 1` over
a single pod would block node drains indefinitely.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Alerts
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/alerts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "slack_webhook_url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX",
    "min_interval_secs": 300,
    "email": {
      "smtp_host": "smtp.example.com",
      "smtp_port": 587,
      "username": "alerts",
      "smtp_password": "app-password",
      "from_address": "alerts@example.com",
      "recipients": ["oncall@example.com"],
      "starttls": true
    }
  }'
```

`GET` returns `slack_webhook_set`, `min_interval_secs` (default 300), and
`email` with `password_set` instead of the password. On `PUT`, omit
`slack_webhook_url` or `smtp_password` to keep it, or set
`clear_slack_webhook` / `clear_smtp_password` to `true` to remove it. Omitting
`email` disables email delivery. `smtp_port` defaults to 587 and `starttls` to
`true`. The test route returns a pass or fail result per channel. See
[Alerting](/docs/operations/alerting).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: API Keys
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/keys` | Create a key; the secret is returned once |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/keys` | List keys (never secrets). `?tenant_id=` restricts to one tenant |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/keys/{id}` | Replace a key's name, description, budget, `weight`, and `max_in_flight` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/keys/{id}` | Delete a key |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/keys/{id}/disabled` | `{"disabled": true}` to disable, `false` to re-enable |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/keys/{id}/tracing` | `{"tracing_enabled": true}` to record spans for this key |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/keys/{id}/usage` | Activity summary for one key |

Create and update bodies:

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | Display name |
| `description` | `""` | Free text |
| `budget_tokens`, `budget_cost_usd` | `null` | Key-level term caps; `null` = uncapped |
| `budget_period` | `null` (`lifetime`) | `lifetime`, `monthly`, or `term` |
| `budget_started_at` | now, when a cap is set | Start of the current term |
| `weight` | `100` | Share of the tenant's capacity relative to its other keys (minimum 1) |
| `max_in_flight` | `null` | Cap on this key's concurrent requests within each model pool |

`PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}` replaces every field: send the current `weight` and
`max_in_flight` to keep them. See
[Fairshare Engine](/docs/concepts/fairshare-engine) for how key weights split a
tenant's share.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenan

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Assistant (Charo)
chunks.text:
`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/settings/charo` carry `enabled` (default `true`; gates the
Playground), `brain_model` (the agent model; `null` for a plain tester),
`tools_enabled` (map of tool name to boolean, for example
`{"run_benchmark": true}`), and benchmark limits `bench_max_concurrency` (40),
`bench_max_duration_s` (120), and `bench_max_requests` (500). `PUT` replaces the
whole object. See [Charo](/docs/guides/charo).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Audit
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/audit` | Most recent audit rows, newest first. `?limit=` (default 100) |

Each row has `id`, `ts`, `actor`, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, and a
`detail` object. See [Audit Log](/docs/operations/audit-log).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Auto router
chunks.text:
| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classifier_enabled` | `false` | Ask a small model for intent tags before routing |
| `classifier_model` | `null` | Registered model used as the classifier; `""` clears it |
| `classifier_timeout_ms` | `250` | On timeout the request routes without tags |
| `capacity_weight` | `0.6` | Weight of spare capacity, clamped to 0–1 |
| `cost_weight` | `0.4` | Weight of cost, clamped to 0–1 |
| `tag_weight` | `0.5` | Weight of tag match, clamped to 0–1 |
| `default_soft_cap` | `8` | Assumed concurrency for models without `max_in_flight`; at least 1 |
| `temperature` | `0.0` | `0` picks the best score; higher samples among candidates; clamped to 0–2 |
| `difficulty_enabled` | `false` | Apply the difficulty tier filter |
| `tier_source` | `hybrid` | `hybrid`, `derived`, or `declared` |
| `messages_default_model` | `null` | Model or `auto` served when a `/v1/messages` request names an unknown model; `""` clears it, and unknown names then get `not_found_error` |

`GET` also returns `available_tags`, the fixed tag vocabulary. The
`OBLETH_AUTO_CLASSIFIER_*` variables only seed these settings on first boot.

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/auto-router \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"classifier_enabled": true, "classifier_model": "qwen3-0.6b", "messages_default_model": "auto"}'
```

`POST /api/v1/router/simulate` takes `prompt` or `messages`, and optionally
`max_

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Backup & Restore
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/backup/export` | Export configuration as JSON |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/backup/restore` | Restore a backup (body limit 64 MiB) |

A backup holds fairshare groups, tenants, keys (hashes only), models,
endpoints, MCP servers, and every `app_settings` row. Upstream secrets are
carried as stored, so they are encrypted when `OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set;
restore checks the backup's `key_check` value and refuses to write if the target's key differs. The
backup also records whether an API-key pepper was set, and restore warns on a
mismatch. Knowledge collections and documents are not included. Restore returns
inserted and updated counts per entity plus `warnings`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/backup/export -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o backup.json

curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/backup/restore \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @backup.json
```

See [Backup & Restore](/docs/operations/backup-restore).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Cache and reliability
chunks.text:
`PUT /api/v1/models/{id}/cache` takes `cache_enabled` and `cache_ttl_secs`
(default 300; `0` disables caching). See
[Response Cache](/docs/guides/response-cache).

`PUT /api/v1/models/{id}/reliability`:

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request_timeout_secs` | `null` | Upstream timeout; `null` uses `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS` (300) |
| `max_retries` | `0` | Extra attempts against the same endpoint after a retryable failure |
| `retry_backoff_ms` | `200` | Base for exponential backoff |
| `endpoint_selection_mode` | `failover` | `failover` (priority order), `load_balance` (weighted), or `session_hash` (conversation-sticky) |
| `debug_diagnostics` | `false` | On a terminal `502`/`504`, record a DNS and TCP probe as a span |

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/reliability \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request_timeout_secs": 60, "max_retries": 2, "retry_backoff_ms": 200, "endpoint_selection_mode": "failover"}'
```

See [Reliability & Failover](/docs/guides/reliability-and-failover).

chunks.heading: Capacity
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Description |

| `GET` | `/api/v1/capacity` | `{"max_in_flight": 1024}`, the global ceiling of the replica that answers |

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Compacting the raw ledger
chunks.text:
`POST /api/v1/usage/compact` drops whole day-partitions of the raw `usage`
table older than the retention window, instead of waiting for the hourly
worker. The daily rollup is never touched.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/usage/compact -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# {"retention_days": 180, "partitions_dropped": 3}
```

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Compression sidecar status
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/settings/compressor` probes the sidecar's `/health` on demand; the
sidecar is configured only by `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL`. It never returns an
error status.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `configured` | `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL` is set |
| `url` | The configured URL; empty when unset |
| `reachable` | The sidecar answered `/health` with `ok` |
| `model`, `revision` | What the sidecar reports |
| `error` | Why a configured sidecar is unreachable |

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Conventions
chunks.text:
**Authentication.** Every route except `GET /api/v1/health`,
`GET /api/v1/version`, and `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` requires the admin token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

The token is compared in constant time. A missing or wrong token returns `401`.
Keep port 9180 on a private network; see [Security](/docs/operations/security).

**Audit actor.** Every mutating call writes an audit row. The actor is taken
from the `X-Obleth-Audit-Actor` header (the dashboard sends the signed-in
user's email; the provisioner sends `system`) and defaults to `admin`.

**Errors.** Failures return JSON `{"error": "<message>"}`:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid body or query (validation message in `error`), including a destination rejected by the outbound URL policy |
| `401` | Missing or wrong admin token |
| `403` | The target is protected (for example the reserved control-plane tenant) |
| `404` | Unknown id. A nested id that belongs to another parent (an endpoint id under the wrong model) is also `404` |
| `409` | Conflict with an existing name |
| `502` | The change was saved in Postgres but the Redis resolver cache could not be updated. The message names `POST /api/v1/resync`; run it to reconcile |

**Secrets are write-only.** Responses never contain an upstream API key, MCP
authorization header, SMTP password, Slack webhook, or Slurm JWT. They report
presence instead: `api_key_set`, `auth_header_set`, `password_se

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Daily usage rollup
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/usage/daily` reads the permanent `usage_daily` rollup, so it
covers dates the raw ledger no longer holds. It backs the **Reports** page and
its CSV export.

| Query param | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start_day` | 7 days ago | Inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `end_day` | today | Inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `tenant_id` | unset | One tenant |
| `key_id` | unset | One key id or a comma-separated list (`key_id=a,b,c`) |
| `model` | unset | One model |
| `group_by` | `day` | `day`, `tenant`, `key`, `model`, or `key_model` |

```bash
curl "http://localhost:9180/api/v1/usage/daily?start_day=2026-08-01&end_day=2026-08-31&group_by=model" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

chunks.heading: Energy accounting
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/energy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": true, "prometheus_url": "http://prometheus:9090", "power_query": "sum by (instance) (node_power_watts)", "poll_interval_secs": 60, "energy_cost_per_kwh": 0.12, "carbon_g_per_kwh": 400.0, "pue": 1.2}'
```

Defaults: `poll_interval_secs` 60, `energy_cost_per_kwh` 0.1,
`carbon_g_per_kwh` 400, `pue` 1.0. `POST /api/v1/settings/energy/test` takes

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Fairshare
chunks.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/fairshare/live` | Live scheduler snapshot of the replica that answers |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/fairshare/history` | Sampled scheduler history for the activity chart |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/fairshare/groups` | Create a group: `{"name", "weight"}` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/fairshare/groups` | List groups |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/fairshare/groups/{name}/weight` | `{"weight": 300}` |

`GET /api/v1/fairshare/live` returns the `algorithm`, the global ceiling
(`max_in_flight`), `default_model_max_in_flight`, global in-flight, queued, and
borrowed counts, and a `pools` array with one entry per model pool (`model`,
`cap`, `in_flight`, `queued`, `borrowed`, and per-group, per-tenant, and
per-key rows with `weight`, `in_flight`, `queued`, `served_tokens`,
`share_score`, `weight_share`, and `expected_slots`; group rows also carry
`slot_cap` and `borrowed`). `share_score` is served tokens divided by weight,
the value the scheduler minimizes: under `weighted`, the tenant with the lowest
score is admitted next, and within a tenant, the key with the lowest score.

`GET /api/v1/fairshare/history` takes `since_ms` (default: the start of the
retention window) and `model` (one pool; absent means all pools summed).

```json
{
  "interval_ms": 2000,
  "retention_ms": 3600000,
  "oldest_ts_ms": 1758625221000,
  "points": [
    {"ts_ms": 1758628821000, "in_flight": 37, "queued": 4, "groups": {"default": 30, "research": 7}}
  ]
}
```

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Lifecycle, schedules, and budgets
chunks.text:
A tenant's `status` gates all of its keys: `active` serves; `suspended` and
`archived` return `403` on the data plane.

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants/$ID/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "suspended"}'
```

Access windows restrict when an active tenant may send traffic, evaluated in
its IANA `timezone` (default `UTC`). In `weekly_windows`, `day` is `0` to `6`
with `0` = Sunday, and `start_min` / `end_min` are minutes from local midnight.

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants/$ID/schedule \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "timezone": "America/Chicago",
    "active_from": "2026-01-12T00:00:00Z",
    "active_until": null,
    "weekly_windows": [{"day": 1, "start_min": 540, "end_min": 1080}]
  }'
```

A term budget caps cumulative usage. `budget_period` is `lifetime` (the
default), `monthly`, or `term`. Set `budget_tokens`, `budget_cost_usd`, or both;
`null` clears a cap. `budget_started_at` defaults to now when a cap is set.
Exhausting either cap returns `403` `tenant term budget exhausted`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants/$ID/budget \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"budget_tokens": 50000000, "budget_cost_usd": 250.0, "budget_period": "monthly"}'
```

See [Quotas & Rate Limits](/docs/guides/quotas-and-rate-limits).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Manifest export and import
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/models/export` returns every model and its endpoints as a JSON
document with `"format": "obleth-models"` and `"version": 1`, sorted by name.
Secrets are never exported; each entry carries `has_api_key` instead, so a
manifest is safe to keep in a repository and to move between instances with
different encryption keys.

Entries are keyed by `model_name`, not `id`, and every other field is
optional: a short file can change one field on one model without touching
anything else. To set an upstream key on import, include `api_key` in plain
text; an entry without it leaves the stored key unchanged.

`POST /api/v1/models/import` merges a manifest: listed models are created or
updated by `model_name`, and models absent from the file are left alone.
Nothing is deleted. All problems in the file are reported together with
`400`. The response counts `created`, `updated`, and `unchanged`, and lists
each model's `action`, `changed_fields`, and `warnings`. Use `?dry_run=true` to
preview.

```bash
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/export -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o models.json

curl -X POST "http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/import?dry_run=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @models.json
```

chunks.text:

curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "search", "upstream_url": "http://mcp-search.example.internal:8080/mcp", "auth_header": "Bearer upstream-token"}'
```

  "id": "66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666",
  "name": "search",

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Model capacity and auto-tune
chunks.text:
`max_in_flight` sets the model's pool size. `capacity_mode` records how it was
chosen: `static` (default, set by an operator) or `tuned` (last written by
auto-tune, with `capacity_tuned_at`).

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/capacity-mode \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"capacity_mode": "static"}'
```

`POST /api/v1/models/{id}/autotune` ramps concurrency directly against the
upstream (bypassing admission) and recommends a `max_in_flight`. It writes no
configuration. `chat` and `embedding` models only.

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workload` | `chat` | `chat` (about 512 prompt and 128 reply tokens) or `coding` (about 6000 and 512) |
| `latency_headroom` | `4.0` | How many times the single-request p99 the model may reach before the ramp calls the knee; clamped to `1.5`–`20` |
| `replicas` | unset | Upstream replica count; sizes the ramp ceiling at 32 per replica |
| `max_concurrency` | `64` | Explicit ceiling; overrides `replicas`; clamped to 512 |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/autotune \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workload": "chat", "latency_headroom": 4.0, "replicas": 2}'
```

The report includes `recommended_max_in_flight`, `knee_reason`
(`latency_degraded`, `plateau`, `max_concurrency`, or `no_data`),
`baseline_p99_ms`, `latency_ceiling_ms`, `recommended_throughp

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Model endpoints
chunks.text:
A model can front several upstreams that serve the same `upstream_model`.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints` | List endpoints |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints` | Add an endpoint |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints/{endpoint_id}` | Update an endpoint |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints/{endpoint_id}` | Remove an endpoint |

An `endpoint_id` that belongs to a different model returns `404`.

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | Unique within the model |
| `api_base` | required | Base URL ending in `/v1`; checked against the outbound URL policy |
| `api_key` | none (the model's key applies) | Write-only. On `PUT`, omit to keep the stored key or send `""` to clear it |
| `priority` | `100` | Lower is tried first in `failover` mode |
| `weight` | `100` | Traffic share in `load_balance` mode |
| `enabled` | `true` | Disabled endpoints leave rotation |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/endpoints \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "cluster-b", "api_base": "http://cluster-b.example.internal:8000/v1", "api_key": "sk-cluster-b", "priority": 200}'
```

```json
{

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Model health
chunks.text:
Health checks settle a model from recent successful traffic when possible,
otherwise from a minimal probe matched to its modality, and finally from the
upstream's model catalog. See [Model Health](/docs/guides/model-health).

`PUT /api/v1/models/{id}/health/config`:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/health/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"checks_enabled": true, "alerts_enabled": true, "check_interval_secs": 900, "failure_threshold": 2, "maintenance_until": null, "maintenance_note": null}'
```

`POST /api/v1/models/health` returns `{"checked": [...], "skipped": N}`.

`POST /api/v1/models/validate` takes `api_base`, `upstream_model`, and
optionally `api_key` and `model_type`. It always returns `200`; an unreachable
upstream is a finding, not an error:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `reachable` | The upstream answered `GET /models` with 2xx |
| `wildcard` | The catalog is a wildcard, so membership cannot be verified |
| `listed` | Whether `upstream_model` is in the catalog; `null` when unknowable |
| `warnings` | Advisories; empty means nothing suspicious |

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The Management API is served by the gateway on the admin listener
(`OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN`, default `0.0.0.0:9180`). It is the only way to change
configuration; the dashboard uses it too. There are 136 method and path
combinations, listed by area below.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Overview summary
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/overview/summary` backs the dashboard's status poll. It takes
`since_ms` and `include_internal`.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `requests`, `tokens`, `cost` | Totals over the window |
| `has_pricing` | Whether any model has a price, so a `0` cost can be told apart from "not priced" |
| `tenant_count`, `active_tenants` | Registered tenants, and how many had traffic in the window |
| `model_count`, `enabled_models` | Registered and enabled models |
| `key_count` | Registered API keys |

If ClickHouse is unavailable the usage totals are zero rather than failing the
response.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Per-key activity summary (bulk)
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/usage/keys/summary` returns one [per-key summary](#per-key-usage-summary)
row for each key with traffic in the window, busiest first. It powers the
**Last used** column on the API Keys page.

| Query param | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `since_ms` | 24 hours ago | Window for the whole scan, including `last_used_ms` |
| `tenant_id` | unset | Restrict to one tenant |
| `limit` | `1000` | Rows returned; capped at `10000` |
| `include_internal` | `false` | Include internal traffic |

Keys idle for the whole window are absent.

```bash
curl "http://localhost:9180/api/v1/usage/keys/summary?tenant_id=$TENANT&since_ms=$(($(date +%s)*1000-2592000000))&limit=5000" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Per-key usage summary
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/keys/{id}/usage` reports when a key was last used, what it last
called, and its rolling totals.

| Query param | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `since_ms` | 24 hours ago | Window for `requests`, token counts, cost, and energy (Unix ms) |
| `include_internal` | `false` | Include health-probe and benchmark traffic |

`last_used_ms` is not bounded by `since_ms`; it is the last use within the
ledger's retention window.

```json
{
  "key_id": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222",
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "last_used_ms": 1758628821000,
  "last_model": "qwen3-8b",
  "last_status_code": 200,
  "requests": 142,
  "input_tokens": 84200,
  "output_tokens": 15600,
  "total_tokens": 99800,
  "cost_usd": 1.24,
  "energy_wh": 96.4,
  "energy_cost_usd": 0.011,
  "co2_g": 38.5
}
```

A key with no traffic returns the same shape with `last_used_ms: 0` and zeroed
totals. An unknown key id returns `404`.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Request logs
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/usage/logs` returns rows from the raw `usage` ledger, newest
first. It powers the **Request Logs** page. Each row is enriched with
`tenant_name`, `key_name`, and `key_prefix` from Postgres.

| Query param | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `since_ms` | 24 hours ago | Inclusive lower bound (Unix ms) |
| `until_ms` | unset | Inclusive upper bound |
| `tenant_id`, `key_id`, `model` | unset | Filters |
| `request_type` | unset | For example `chat`, `messages`, `embedding`; see [ClickHouse Usage](/docs/reference/clickhouse-usage#request-types) |
| `session_id` | unset | Exact match |
| `device_id` | unset | Exact match on the device id recorded for identity-token traffic |
| `status` | unset | `success` (2xx and 3xx) or `error` (400 and above) |
| `request_id` | unset | Case-insensitive prefix match |
| `before_ms`, `before_request_id` | unset | Keyset cursor for the next, older page |
| `traced_only` | `false` | Only requests that recorded spans |
| `include_internal` | `false` | Include internal traffic |
| `limit` | `50` | Page size, clamped to 1 to 200 |

```bash
curl "http://localhost:9180/api/v1/usage/logs?since_ms=$(($(date +%s)*1000-3600000))&tenant_id=$TENANT&request_type=chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Request spans
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/usage/logs/{request_id}/spans` returns every span recorded for one
request, ordered by `start_ms`; the array is empty when the request was not
traced. Spans are kept for 14 days.

```json
[
  {
    "request_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "span_name": "proxy_request",
    "parent_span": "",
    "start_ms": 1758628821000,
    "duration_ms": 1243,
    "status": "ok",
    "attributes": "{}"
  },
  {
    "request_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "span_name": "upstream",
    "parent_span": "proxy_request",
    "start_ms": 1758628821010,
    "duration_ms": 1180,
    "status": "ok",
    "attributes": "{}"
  }
]
```

See [Observability](/docs/operations/observability#per-request-span-tracing)
for the span names.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Slurm provisioner
chunks.text:
System-wide Slurm connection settings used by `obleth-provisioner`. See
[Slurm Provisioning](/docs/guides/slurm-provisioning).

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/slurm \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "slurmrestd_url": "http://slurm.example.internal:6820",
    "slurmrestd_api_version": "v0.0.40",
    "slurm_user": "obleth",
    "slurm_jwt": "<jwt>",
    "node_aliases": [{"host": "gpu-node-01", "ip": "10.0.0.10"}]
  }'
```

`PUT` replaces `enabled`, `slurmrestd_url`, `slurm_user`, and `node_aliases`
(send the full list; blank rows are dropped and a non-IP address is rejected).
Omit `slurm_jwt` or send it empty to keep the stored JWT, which is encrypted
at rest. `slurmrestd_api_version` defaults to `v0.0.40`.

`GET` returns `jwt_set` and `jwt_last4` instead of the JWT, plus provisioner
status: `provisioner_running`, `provisioner_last_seen_secs`,
`provisioner_version`, `provisioner_git_sha`, `provisioner_built_at`,
`provisioner_tick_status` (`ok`, `idle`, or `error`),
`provisioner_tick_detail`, `provisioner_last_ok_secs`, and
`provisioner_held_secs`.

`POST /api/v1/settings/slurm/test` returns:

```json

  "jwt": {"set": true, "expired": false, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z", "expires_in_secs": 5961600},
  "ping": {"ok": true, "status_code": 200, "latency_ms": 12, "error": null}
}
```

the pr

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Time series
chunks.text:
The three series routes take `since_ms`, `bucket_ms` (default `300000`, minimum
`10000`), `tenant_id`, `model` (required for `/series/models`), and
`include_internal`. A series never returns more than 5000 buckets: when the
window divided by `bucket_ms` would exceed that, the bucket width is widened
until it fits.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Usage retention
chunks.text:
```bash
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/usage-retention -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# {"days": 180, "configured": false}

curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/usage-retention \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"days": 90}'

```

`days` must be between 1 and 36500. `configured: false` means the value comes
from `OBLETH_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`. The daily rollup is never pruned.

chunks.title: Postgres Schema

chunks.text:
Only the hash of a key's secret is stored. An
[identity key](/docs/guides/identity-tokens) (`kind = 'identity'`) has no
secret: its `key_hash` is `jwt:` followed by the hex SHA-256 of the issuer, a
NUL byte, and the subject, so the data plane resolves it with the same lookup.

| Column | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `UUID` PRIMARY KEY | |

| `name` | `TEXT` NOT NULL | |
| `description` | `TEXT` NOT NULL DEFAULT `''` | |
| `key_prefix` | `TEXT` NOT NULL | First 18 characters, safe to display |
| `key_hash` | `TEXT` NOT NULL UNIQUE | SHA-256 of the secret (peppered when `OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER` is set), or the `jwt:` handle |
| `kind` | `TEXT` NOT NULL DEFAULT `'secret'` | `secret` or `identity` |
| `identity_issuer`, `identity_subject` | `TEXT` | Identity keys only |
| `identity_claims` | `JSONB` | Claims captured at first use; identity keys only |
| `budget_tokens`, `budget_cost_usd`, `budget_period`, `budget_started_at` | | Key-level term budget, same meaning as on `tenants` |
| `weight` | `BIGINT` NOT NULL DEFAULT `100` | Share of the tenant's capacity relative to its other keys (at least 1) |
| `max_in_flight` | `BIGINT` | Cap on this key's concurrent requests within each model pool |
| `disabled` | `BOOLEAN` NOT NULL DEFAULT `false` | |
| `tracing_enabled` | `BOOLEAN` NOT NULL DEFAULT `false` | Record spans for this key |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | |

Indexed by `t

role, status from "user";`).

chunks.title: Postgres Schema
chunks.heading: Migrations
chunks.text:
The gateway's schema lives in `schema/postgres/` and is compiled into the
`obleth` binary. On every boot the gateway applies all 25 files in order, under
a Postgres advisory lock so concurrent replicas do not race. Every statement is
idempotent (`create … if not exists`, `add column if not exists`, guarded
constraints), so re-applying against an existing database is safe. There is no
migration-version table.

| File | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `0001_init.sql` | Initial schema: `fairshare_groups`, `tenants`, `api_keys`, `audit_log`, `models`, `model_health_checks`, `model_endpoints`, `managed_models`, `model_replicas`, `mcp_servers`, `app_settings` |
| `0002_tracing_flag.sql` | `tracing_enabled` on `tenants` and `api_keys` |
| `0003_guardrails_policy.sql` | `guardrails_policy` on `tenants` |
| `0004_saved_recipes.sql` | An earlier launch-preset table, replaced and dropped by `0006` |
| `0005_managed_launcher_spec.sql` | `launcher_spec` on `managed_models` |
| `0006_recipes.sql` | `recipes` table |
| `0007_replica_port_and_min_replicas.sql` | `port_base` on `model_replicas`, `min_replicas` on `managed_models` |
| `0008_managed_provision_error.sql` | `last_provision_error`, `last_provision_error_at` on `managed_models` |
| `0009_replica_cancel_requested.sql` | `cancel_requested` on `model_replicas` |
| `0010_drop_replica_model_cascade.sql` | Drops the `model_replicas` → `models` foreign key so replica rows outlive their model and the provisioner can still cancel their jobs |

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: Example queries
chunks.text:
Client request rate by admission class:

```promql
sum by (admission) (rate(obleth_requests_total{admission!="boon"}[5m]))
```

Share of client requests that had to queue:

```promql
sum(rate(obleth_requests_total{admission="queued"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(obleth_requests_total{admission!="boon"}[5m]))
```

P95 time to first token:

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(obleth_ttft_ms_bucket[5m])))
```

Response-cache hit rate:

```promql
sum(rate(obleth_cache_lookups_total{result="hit"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(obleth_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
```

Upstream failures that reached clients:

```promql
sum(rate(obleth_upstream_attempts_total{outcome="exhausted"}[5m]))
```

Lost usage rows (alert on any increase):

```promql
increase(obleth_telemetry_dropped[15m]) > 0
```

Knowledge embedder outages:

```promql
sum(rate(obleth_knowledge_retrievals_total{outcome="error"}[5m]))
```

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: Metric details
chunks.text:
Each metric has its own anchor, for example
`/docs/reference/prometheus-metrics#obleth_jwt_verify_total`.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: Metric reference
chunks.text:
| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `obleth_requests_total` | Counter | `admission`, `status` | Requests by admission class and status class |
| `obleth_input_tokens_total` | Counter | | Input tokens across all recorded requests |
| `obleth_output_tokens_total` | Counter | | Output tokens across all recorded requests |
| `obleth_ttft_ms` | Histogram | | Time to first token, in ms |
| `obleth_total_ms` | Histogram | | Total request duration, in ms |
| `obleth_in_flight` | Gauge | | Requests currently holding a fairshare slot |
| `obleth_queue_depth` | Gauge | | Requests waiting for admission |
| `obleth_telemetry_dropped` | Gauge | | Usage records lost since the process started |
| `obleth_cache_lookups_total` | Counter | `result` | Response-cache lookups by result |
| `obleth_cache_tokens_saved_total` | Counter | | Tokens served from the response cache instead of the upstream |
| `obleth_compression_tokens_saved_total` | Counter | | Input tokens removed by the compression boon before dispatch |
| `obleth_mcp_requests_total` | Counter | `server`, `status` | MCP gateway requests by server and status class |
| `obleth_upstream_attempts_total` | Counter | `outcome` | Upstream dispatch attempts by outcome |
| `obleth_jwt_verify_total` | Counter | `result` | JWT bearer verification outcomes |
| `obleth_jwks_refresh_total` | Counter | `issuer_index`, `result` | JWKS fetch outcomes per configured issuer |
| `obleth_knowledge_retrievals_total` | Counte

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_cache_lookups_total`
chunks.text: `result` is `hit` or `miss`.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_cache_tokens_saved_total`
chunks.text: On a cache hit, grows by the cached response's tokens.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_compression_tokens_saved_total`
chunks.text:
Input tokens removed by the [compression boon](/docs/guides/model-boons) before
dispatch.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_in_flight`
chunks.text:
Read from the fairshare scheduler at scrape time; covers every model pool in
the process.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_input_tokens_total`
chunks.text: Input tokens of every recorded request, including boon helper calls.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_jwks_refresh_total`
chunks.text:
`issuer_index` is the issuer's position in `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS`, starting at 0;
`result` is `ok` or `error`. A sustained `error` rate means the gateway is
verifying against its last good key set and will reject tokens signed with a
newly rotated key.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_jwt_verify_total`
chunks.text:
`result` is `ok` or a rejection reason: `unknown_issuer`, `bad_alg`,
`unknown_kid`, `bad_signature`, `expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `bad_audience`,
`bad_subject`, or `malformed`. A verified token that cannot be mapped to an
identity key also counts `not_provisioned` or `provision_failed`. Those two are
counted in addition to `ok`, so rejections are the total minus `ok`, not the
sum of the other labels. See [Identity Tokens](/docs/guides/identity-tokens).

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_knowledge_retrievals_total`
chunks.text:
Counted once per chat request to a model with the `knowledge` boon.

| `outcome` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hit` | Chunks scored above the minimum and were injected |
| `miss` | Retrieval ran but nothing was injected (no chunk met the score threshold, no attached collection had data, or no room in the context budget) |
| `no_query` | The request had no user text to search with |
| `no_window` | The model has no context window configured, so the injection budget cannot be computed |
| `error` | Every embedding attempt for a collection with data failed, for example an unreachable or timed-out embedder |

See [Knowledge Base (RAG)](/docs/guides/knowledge-base).

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_mcp_requests_total`

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_output_tokens_total`
chunks.text: Output tokens of every recorded request, including boon helper calls.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_queue_depth`
chunks.text: Requests waiting for a slot in any model pool, read at scrape time.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_requests_total`
chunks.text:
| Label | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `admission` | `fast` (admitted immediately), `queued` (admitted after waiting), `rejected` (budget exhausted or fail-closed), `boon` (a helper call made by a boon, such as a vision describer or structured-output fixer) |
| `status` | status class: `2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`, and so on |

`boon` samples always report `2xx` and add their tokens to the token counters.
To count client requests only, exclude them:
`obleth_requests_total{admission!="boon"}`.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_telemetry_dropped`
chunks.text:
A running count of usage records that never reached ClickHouse or the
write-ahead log. A record is dropped when the in-memory telemetry buffer is
full, or when a batch that failed to insert could not be written to the WAL
either (disk or segment cap). Records spilled to the WAL are not dropped; they
replay when ClickHouse recovers. Any increase means lost usage rows. See
[Observability](/docs/operations/observability).

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: `obleth_upstream_attempts_total`
chunks.text:
| `outcome` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `success` | The attempt produced a usable response |
| `retry` | Retryable failure; a configured retry remains on this endpoint |
| `conn_retry` | Connection-level send failure (for example a stale pooled socket) after the configured retries are spent; one extra attempt on a fresh connection after 50 ms |
| `timeout` | The attempt hit the request timeout |
| `failover` | The endpoint was exhausted and dispatch moved to the next endpoint |
| `exhausted` | Every endpoint and attempt failed; the client received `502` or `504` and was not billed |

See [Reliability & Failover](/docs/guides/reliability-and-failover).

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The gateway serves Prometheus text format at `/metrics` on the metrics listener
(`OBLETH_METRICS_LISTEN`, default `0.0.0.0:9091`). There are 16 metrics, all
prefixed `obleth_`. Labels are deliberately low-cardinality: no tenant, key,
model, or collection appears as a label. Per-tenant and per-model breakdowns
come from the [ClickHouse usage ledger](/docs/reference/clickhouse-usage).

Each gateway process exports its own values. With several replicas, aggregate
with `sum()` across the scrape targets.

chunks.title: Prometheus Metrics
chunks.heading: Scrape configuration
chunks.text:
```yaml
# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: obleth
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["obleth:9091"]
```

The Compose `observability` profile ships this configuration, plus jobs for the
Postgres and Redis exporters, ClickHouse (`9363`), and HAProxy (`8404`). With
the Prometheus Operator, set `serviceMonitor.enabled: true` in the Helm chart;
the rendered ServiceMonitor scrapes the `metrics` port every 5 s.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Budget scripts
chunks.text:
All budget changes run as Lua scripts, so they are atomic across gateway
replicas:

| Script | Keys | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RESERVE` | bucket | Refills the per-minute bucket for the elapsed time, then reserves the estimate. A `tokens_per_minute` of 0 means no per-minute cap |
| `RESERVE_WITH_TERM` | bucket, term usage, term reserved | Checks the term cap against committed plus reserved usage, reserves from the bucket, and records the term reservation, in one round trip. Returns reserved, bucket exhausted, or term exhausted |
| `RECONCILE` | bucket | Applies the difference between the estimate and the actual cost |
| `TERM_USAGE_READ` / `TERM_USAGE_ADD` | term usage | Read or add to the committed counters, resetting them when the period changes |
| `TERM_RECONCILE` | term usage, term reserved | Releases a reservation and commits the actual usage exactly once |

The bucket refills continuously at `tokens_per_minute / 60000` tokens per
millisecond up to its capacity. An estimate larger than the whole bucket is
admitted when the bucket is full and runs into bounded debt (floor
`-capacity`) instead of being rejected forever.

The term gate runs before the bucket, so a request rejected for its term budget
never holds bucket tokens. Rejections return:

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-minute bucket exhausted | `429` | `token budget exceeded` |
| Tenant term budget exhausted | `403` | `tenant term budget exhausted` |
| Key term budget exhausted | `40

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Eviction
chunks.text:
The bundled Helm Redis runs with `--maxmemory` (default `400mb`) and
`--maxmemory-policy volatile-lru`, so only keys with a TTL can be evicted.
Resolver entries have no TTL and are never evicted. The bundled Compose Redis
sets no memory limit. On an external Redis, use a `volatile-*` policy or
`noeviction`; an `allkeys-*` policy can evict resolver entries, which then fail
with `401` until the next re-warm.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Invalidation channel
chunks.text:
Management API writes publish a target on the pub/sub channel
`obleth:invalidate`. Every gateway replica drops the matching entry from its
in-process cache (a 300-second TTL layer in front of Redis), so the next
request reads the new value from Redis.

| Payload | Drops |
| --- | --- |
| `*` | every in-process entry |
| `model:<name>` | one model route |
| `mcp:<name>` | one MCP server |
| any other value | the API key with that hash |

Messages published while a replica's subscription is down are lost, so after
resubscribing the replica drops its whole in-process cache and re-warms Redis
from Postgres (see below).

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Key prefixes
chunks.text:
| Key | Type | TTL | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `obleth:key:<hash>` | String | none | `ResolvedKey` JSON for one API key, keyed by the key's SHA-256 hash. JWT identity keys use `jwt:` followed by a SHA-256 of issuer and subject |
| `obleth:model:<name>` | String | none | Resolved model route JSON, written once per addressable name: the canonical name and every alias |
| `obleth:mcp:<name>` | String | none | Resolved MCP server JSON |
| `obleth:budget:<tenant_id>` | Hash | 10 min, re-armed on every reserve and reconcile | Per-minute token bucket: `tokens`, `ts` (last refill, ms) |
| `obleth:term_usage:<scope>` | Hash | 1 year, re-armed on every write | Committed term-budget usage: `period`, `tokens`, `cost`. `<scope>` is a tenant id or, for key-level budgets, a key id |
| `obleth:term_reserved:<scope>` | Hash | 10 min, set on creation, never re-armed | In-flight term-budget reservations: `period`, `tokens`, `cost` |
| `obleth:cache:<sha256>` | String | the model's `cache_ttl_secs` | Cached response (status, content type, body, token counts) |
| `obleth:compress:<tenant_id>:<sha256>` | String | Settings → Compression original TTL (default 3600 s) | Original text stashed by the compression boon so it can be retrieved |
| `obleth:knowledge:q:<hash>` | String (binary) | Settings → Knowledge query cache TTL (default 600 s) | Cached query embedding for knowledge retrieval: the vector as little-endian `f32` bytes, keyed by a SHA-256 of the embedding model and query text.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Redis holds the data plane's hot state: the resolver cache for API keys, models,
and MCP servers, the per-minute and term budget counters, the response cache,
and a few small caches used by boons and the provisioner. Postgres remains the
source of truth for configuration; the resolver entries are rebuilt from it
automatically.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Rebuilding from Postgres
chunks.text:
Resolver entries have no TTL, so obleth keeps them in step with Postgres in
four ways:

1. **Startup.** Each gateway process pushes every key, model, and MCP server
   into Redis during boot.
2. **Every write.** Management API mutations update or delete the entry and
   publish an invalidation.
3. **Re-warm.** Every `OBLETH_REDIS_REWARM_SECS` (default 300) and after every
   Redis reconnect, the gateway pushes a fresh Postgres snapshot and prunes
   stale entries. A Redis restart or flush heals without restarting the
   gateway.
4. **Resync.** `POST /api/v1/resync` (Settings → Data → **Reconcile cache**)
   runs the same push and prune on demand and returns counts per namespace.
   Use it after a delete that reported a failed eviction.

The prune SCANs `obleth:key:*`, `obleth:model:*`, and `obleth:mcp:*` and
deletes every entry that is not in the snapshot, so a revoked key or deleted
model cannot keep resolving. It then re-reads Postgres once more and restores
anything created between the snapshot and the SCAN.

The data plane does not read Postgres on the request path: a key that is not in
Redis returns `401` until the entry is written back.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Requirements
chunks.text:
- **Authentication is required.** The request path reads API keys from Redis,
  so an unauthenticated instance would let anyone who reaches it mint keys.
  Connect with `OBLETH_REDIS_URL=redis://:PASSWORD@host:6379`. The bundled
  Compose and Helm Redis always run with `--requirepass`.
- **A single primary.** Point obleth at one Redis primary. A managed endpoint
  that fails over but always presents a single primary is fine. A sharded
  keyspace is not supported: the budget scripts touch several keys in one call
  (`RESERVE_WITH_TERM` reads the bucket, the term-usage hash, and the
  reservation hash together), and the gateway's Redis client is built without
  cluster support.
- **Timeouts.** Each command waits at most `OBLETH_REDIS_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`
  (250 ms) and each connect at most `OBLETH_REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`
  (2000 ms). A timed-out budget operation is handled by `OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN`. A
  failed API-key lookup returns `503` rather than `401`.

To inspect a running instance:

```bash
redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" --no-auth-warning --scan --pattern 'obleth:model:*'
```

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: ResolvedKey
chunks.text:
Everything admission needs is in one JSON value, so the hot path makes no
relational lookup:

```json
{
  "key_id": "661f9500-...",
  "tenant_id": "550e8400-...",
  "tenant_name": "chatbot",
  "fairshare_group": "default",
  "group_weight": 100,
  "weight": 100,
  "tokens_per_minute": 50000,
  "max_in_flight": null,
  "disabled": false,
  "status": "active",
  "timezone": "UTC",
  "active_from": null,
  "active_until": null,
  "weekly_windows": null,
  "budget_tokens": null,
  "budget_cost_usd": null,
  "budget_period": null,
  "budget_started_at": null,
  "key_budget_tokens": null,
  "key_budget_cost_usd": null,
  "key_budget_period": null,
  "key_budget_started_at": null,
  "key_weight": 100,
  "key_max_in_flight": null,
  "allowed_models": null,
  "internal": false,
  "tracing_enabled": false,
  "guardrails_policy": null,
  "compression_policy": null,
  "synthetic": false
}
```

`weight` and `max_in_flight` are the tenant's. `key_weight` splits the tenant's
share among its keys, and `key_max_in_flight` caps one key inside each model
pool. `internal` marks gateway-owned traffic such as health probes;
`synthetic` marks a tenant whose traffic is recorded as benchmark traffic.

chunks.title: Redis Layout
chunks.heading: Response cache key
chunks.text:
`obleth:cache:<sha256>` is a SHA-256 over the tenant id, the model, and the raw
request body, separated by zero bytes. Two requests share an entry only when
all three match. A model caches only when `cache_enabled` is true and
`cache_ttl_secs` is greater than 0; responses over 512 KiB are not cached. See
[Response Cache](/docs/guides/response-cache).
